sections.title: Week 22 · The Message About the Pool
sections.text: A neighbourhood chat reported that the small swimming pool was closing permanently. The claim began after an instructor told a parent that lessons would stop during roof repairs. The parent wrote, 'She said the pool would close next month.' Another member removed the time reference when forwarding the message. By evening, several families had cancelled future bookings. The manager asked who had announced a permanent closure. Nobody could identify such a statement. She explained that the building would close for twelve days and asked families to check the official timetable before changing plans. The instructor confirmed that she had meant a temporary pause. A student reporter interviewed both speakers and published their words with dates. The correction did not accuse the parent of inventing the entire story; it showed how an accurate detail had lost an essential limit as it travelled.

sections.text: A repair cafe depends on more than the person who holds the screwdriver. Our team includes a volunteer who welcomes visitors and a coordinator who keeps each item with its paperwork. The objects that arrive often carry stories as well as faults. Last week, a lamp that belonged to a retired teacher needed a new switch. The volunteer who assessed it asked about its history before discussing the repair. That conversation did not replace technical judgement, but it helped explain why the owner preferred repair to replacement. We also need a system that records limits honestly. Items that cannot be repaired safely are returned with an explanation, not a vague promise. Some visitors are disappointed, yet clear boundaries protect trust. The most useful volunteer is not always the one who says yes fastest. It may be the person who asks the question that prevents a well-intentioned but unsuitable repair.

sections.text: Our town archive is collecting stories from traders whose families have worked in the market for generations. The project began in the cafe where several retired sellers meet every Thursday. One woman remembers the winter when the old roof collapsed under heavy snow. Another recalls the year when refrigerated vans changed the fish trade. These memories connect personal experience with changes in the town, but dates sometimes conflict. The archivist records uncertainty rather than forcing every account into one neat timeline. A photograph whose owner is unknown can still be useful if its limits are stated. The team asks contributors to explain where their knowledge comes from: direct experience, a relative's story or a later newspaper report. This does not make the interviews less warm. It makes the archive more trustworthy. A market is a place where stories travel quickly; an archive is a place where they should also arrive with a source.

Host: Do you remember the day when you met her?
Designer: Yes. I brought a chair whose legs looked elegant but were unstable. She asked who would actually sit on it.

Designer: Exactly. Farida didn't give me a perfect design. She showed me a place where I could ask better questions. My chair stopped being a drawing that expected humans to adapt politely to it.

sections.text: The volunteer who arrived late to our planning meeting became the person we most needed. Kamila, who works at a bus depot, noticed that our event timetable ignored the last service to the northern neighbourhoods. The schedule we had prepared looked convenient for the organising team, but several visitors would have struggled to get home. Our chair suggested simply telling people to leave early. Kamila argued that they should not have to miss the final discussion because of where they lived. We moved the closing session forward and kept an optional social hour afterwards. The change, which cost nothing, made the event more accessible. It also challenged our assumption that useful planning knowledge comes only from senior organisers. Kamila had no formal role in transport policy. She knew the route people used every evening. The person who notices an ordinary practical detail may contribute more than the person whose presentation has the most impressive title.

sections.text: People waiting outside the community clinic had no shelter during last month's rain. A temporary canopy installed near the entrance now offers some protection. The clinic also introduced numbered cards, which reduced arguments about places in the queue. However, the new system created another problem: visitors unable to hear the number calls sometimes missed their turn. A volunteer suggested a visual display showing the current number. Staff tested a simple whiteboard before buying equipment, which allowed them to discover practical issues cheaply. The board placed behind the reception glass reflected light and was difficult to read. Moving it beside the door solved much of the problem. These changes show that an improvement can help one group while overlooking another. The team now asks visitors using different communication methods to test each stage. A fair queue is not created merely by giving everyone a number; people also need a reliable way to know when that number matters.

sections.text: The first park survey reached people who already attended weekend events. Residents whose working hours included Saturdays were largely absent. The committee initially called the results representative, which overstated what the evidence could show. We redesigned the survey with short interviews at the bus stop where commuters waited and a paper version delivered to nearby buildings. Responses collected through the new routes raised different priorities: lighting, toilets and weekday seating mattered more than another festival stage. This did not make the first respondents wrong. It showed that the people we had asked were only part of the community. The report now explains each collection method and the groups still missing from the sample. The council officer to whom we sent it requested a follow-up discussion. A survey becomes more credible when it admits its limits. The most polished chart cannot give a voice to residents who were never asked a question in the first place.

questions.prompt: Ikki daqiqada so‘rov tanlanmasi yoki film qulayligini tanqidiy baholang va tekshirish rejasini bering.
criteria: Uch xil relative tuzilma to‘g‘ri.
Chetda qolgan guruh aniq.
Dalilga mos cheklangan xulosa va taklif bor.

questions.prompt: Shahar bog‘i bo‘yicha mas’ul Mr Ahmed ga 120–150 so‘zli rasmiy email yozing: dastlabki so‘rov cheklovi, yangi dalillar va muhokama uchun ikki aniq talab.
expected:
Dear Mr Ahmed,
I am writing about the park survey that our committee recently revised. The original responses came mainly from people who attend Saturday events. Residents whose jobs keep them busy at weekends were not adequately represented, which limited the conclusions we could draw.
We have now added interviews at the bus stop where commuters wait and paper forms delivered to nearby buildings. The responses collected through these routes place greater emphasis on lighting, toilets and weekday seating.
Could you arrange a meeting to review these priorities before the next spending decision? We would also appreciate information about groups that the council believes are still missing from the survey. The report, which explains both collection methods, is ready for discussion.
Thank you for considering a broader evidence base rather than treating the first chart as a complete picture.
Yours sincerely,
Malika Saidova
criteria: 120–150 so‘z; oluvchi, maqsad va rasmiy yakun bor.
Uchrashuv va yetishmayotgan guruhlar haqida ikki so‘rov.
Kamida uch relative shakli ma’noga mos.

questions.prompt: Odamni aniqlovchi olmoshni tanlang; faqat javobni yozing: The nurse ___ treated my ankle was very gentle. (who / which)
questions.explanation: Nurse odamni bildiradi, shuning uchun berilgan variantlardan who mos keladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat xato olmoshni almashtirib, butun gapni yozing. Who ishlating: Do you know the chef which won the prize?
expected: Do you know the chef who won the prize?
questions.explanation: Chef odam bo‘lgani uchun which emas, who kerak. Who ergash gapning egasi ham hisoblanadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Odamni aniqlang; who/which: The volunteer ___ teaches chess also runs the club.
questions.explanation: Who odamni aniqlovchi nisbiy olmoshdir.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Odamga who ishlating: The driver which helped us was very calm.
expected: The driver who helped us was very calm.
questions.explanation: Driver shaxs bo‘lgani uchun who mos.

questions.prompt: Who bilan birlashtiring; is my aunt bilan tugating: The woman is my aunt. She owns the bakery.
expected: The woman who owns the bakery is my aunt.
questions.explanation: Who owns the bakery qaysi ayol ekanini aniqlaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “The students who arrive early can choose their seats” kimlarga tegishli? A) Erta keladigan talabalarga. B) Barcha talabalarga, kelishidan qat’i nazar.
questions.explanation: Defining relative guruhni chegaralaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat mos olmoshni yozing: The battery ___ powers this sensor is tiny. (which / who)
questions.explanation: Battery narsa bo‘lgani uchun which qo‘llanadi. Bu aniqlovchi gapda that ham mumkin, ammo variantlarda which berilgan.

questions.prompt: Bo‘shliqqa which yoki that dan mos keladiganini yozing: Is this the cable ___ connects the printer to the laptop?
questions.explanation: Narsani aniqlovchi defining relative gapda which ham, that ham ishlatilishi mumkin.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Buyumni aniqlang; which/that dan foydalaning: The lamp ___ stands by the sofa is solar-powered.
questions.explanation: Buyum uchun defining relative da which yoki that ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Olmoshni tuzating, which ishlating: The software who controls the heating has failed.
expected: The software which controls the heating has failed.
questions.explanation: Software shaxs emas, shuning uchun which kerak.

questions.prompt: That bilan birlashtiring: The jacket is waterproof. I bought it yesterday.
expected: The jacket that I bought yesterday is waterproof.
questions.explanation: That I bought yesterday buyumni aniqlaydi; it tushadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “The key that opens the cellar is rusty” gapida that nimaga ishora qiladi? A) Cellar ga. B) Key ga.
questions.explanation: Nisbiy qism key otini aniqlaydi.

questions.prompt: Egalikni bildiruvchi bitta nisbiy olmoshni yozing: The athlete ___ coach retired is looking for a new trainer.
questions.explanation: Murabbiy sportchiga tegishli ekanini whose coach birikmasi ko‘rsatadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat mos so‘zni yozing: Have you met the artist ___ paintings hang in the lobby? (who / whose)
questions.explanation: Paintings oldidan egalik bildiruvchi whose kerak: rasmlari vestibyulda osilgan rassom.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Egalik: The woman ___ bicycle was stolen called the police.
questions.explanation: Whose keyingi otning egasini bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Egalik olmoshi: The singer who's voice we heard is Uzbek.
expected: The singer whose voice we heard is Uzbek.
questions.explanation: Whose egalik; who’s esa who is yoki who has.

questions.prompt: Whose bilan birlashtiring: I met a boy. His father repairs clocks.
expected: I met a boy whose father repairs clocks.
questions.explanation: His father o‘rniga whose father keladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “The tree whose branches broke is very old” gapida whose buyumga ishlatilishi mumkinmi? A) Ha. B) Yo‘q, faqat odamlarga.
questions.explanation: Whose odamlar bilan birga buyumlarning egaligini ham ko‘rsatadi.

questions.prompt: Joyni ifodalovchi where yoki which ni tanlang: We found a café ___ cyclists can refill their bottles. Faqat so‘zni yozing.
questions.explanation: Ergash gap kafeda sodir bo‘ladigan harakatni bildiradi; where bu yerda at which ma’nosida.

questions.prompt: Faqat bitta so‘zni tuzating va butun gapni yozing: This is the studio which we record our podcast. Which o‘rniga joy ravishini qo‘ying.
expected: This is the studio where we record our podcast.
questions.explanation: We record our podcast gapiga joy ma’nosi kerak. Where — in which, ya’ni o‘sha studiyada degani.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Joy ravishi, where/which: This is the warehouse ___ we store the spare parts.
questions.explanation: Where joyda bajariladigan ishni bog‘laydi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Takroriy joy predlogini olib tashlang: This is the park where we play in.
expected: This is the park where we play.
questions.explanation: Where bu yerda in the park ma’nosini o‘z ichiga oladi.

questions.prompt: Where bilan birlashtiring; is tiny bilan tugating: The village is tiny. My grandparents live there.
expected: The village where my grandparents live is tiny.
questions.explanation: There o‘rnini where egallaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “the shop where I work” qaysi iboraga teng? A) the shop which I work B) the shop in which I work
questions.explanation: Where bu yerda in which bilan teng.

questions.prompt: Faqat mos so‘zni yozing: Do you recall the winter ___ the lake froze completely? (when / where)
questions.explanation: Winter vaqtni bildiradi; shu davrda sodir bo‘lgan hodisa when bilan bog‘lanadi.

questions.prompt: Vaqtni bildiruvchi nisbiy ravishni yozing: There was a period ___ our village had no electricity. (when / whose)
questions.explanation: Period vaqt oralig‘i. When ergash gapni shu davr bilan bog‘laydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Vaqt ravishi: I still remember the evening ___ the power failed. (when / where)
questions.explanation: Evening vaqtni bildiradi; when mos.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Vaqtga mos ravish: July was the month where we moved house.
expected: July was the month when we moved house.
questions.explanation: Month bilan vaqt ravishi when ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: When bilan birlashtiring: I remember the morning. We found the lost puppy then.
expected: I remember the morning when we found the lost puppy.
questions.explanation: Then o‘rnini when egallaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “the year when I graduated” gapida when nimani bog‘laydi? A) Bitirgan vaqtni. B) Bitirgan joyni.
questions.explanation: When vaqt nisbiy gapini kiritadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Qaysi gapda zarur ega olmoshi bor? A) The dog that guards the warehouse belongs to Aziz. B) The dog guards the warehouse belongs to Aziz.
questions.explanation: That guards fe’lining egasi bo‘lib kelgan. Ega vazifasidagi nisbiy olmoshni tushirib bo‘lmaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. To‘g‘ri savolni tanlang: A) Where is the parcel arrived this morning? B) Where is the parcel that arrived this morning?
questions.explanation: Arrived fe’lining egasi that. Uni olib tashlash ikki gapni grammatik bog‘lovchisiz qoldiradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Tushirib bo‘lmaydigan ega olmoshi, who/which: The architect ___ designed this library won an award.
questions.explanation: Who designed qismining egasi; uni tushirib bo‘lmaydi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Yetishmayotgan that ni qo‘shing: The bus stops outside our house is always crowded.
expected: The bus that stops outside our house is always crowded.
questions.explanation: That stops qismida that ega bo‘lib zarur.

questions.prompt: Takroriy he ni olib tashlang: The man who he delivers our bread is on holiday.
expected: The man who delivers our bread is on holiday.
questions.explanation: Who allaqachon ega, yana he kerak emas.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Qaysi gapda which ni tushirib bo‘lmaydi? A) The camera which I use is old. B) The camera which fell is broken.
questions.explanation: Which fell da which ega; I use da esa to‘ldiruvchi.

questions.prompt: Faqat to‘ldiruvchi nisbiy olmoshini olib tashlab, gapni qayta yozing: The recipe that you recommended was delicious.
expected: The recipe you recommended was delicious.
questions.explanation: That recommended fe’lining to‘ldiruvchisi; ega you bo‘lgani uchun that ni tushirish mumkin.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Qaysi gapda nisbiy olmoshni tushirish mumkin? A) The scarf which I knitted is green. B) The scarf which covers the statue is green.
questions.explanation: A da which to‘ldiruvchi, I esa ega. B da which covers fe’lining egasi, shuning uchun tushirilmaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Nisbiy olmosh tushirilgan: The person ___ I hired starts tomorrow. (who / zero) Ikkalasi mumkin bo‘lsa both yozing.
questions.explanation: Defining gapda to‘ldiruvchi who tushirilishi mumkin.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Ortiqcha it ni olib tashlang: The song I heard it yesterday is beautiful.
expected: The song I heard yesterday is beautiful.
questions.explanation: Song nisbiy qismning to‘ldiruvchisi, it takrorlanmaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat to‘ldiruvchi olmoshni olib tashlang: The hotel that you suggested has closed.
expected: The hotel you suggested has closed.
questions.explanation: You ega bo‘lgani uchun object that tushiriladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “The doctor I saw was helpful” gapida tushirilgan olmoshning vazifasi: A) To‘ldiruvchi. B) Ega.
questions.explanation: I ega, doctor esa saw fe’lining to‘ldiruvchisidir.

questions.prompt: Faqat mos olmoshni yozing: Dr Evans, ___ trained in Canada, now runs our clinic. (who / that)
questions.explanation: Vergul bilan ajratilgan qo‘shimcha ma’lumot gapida odam uchun who ishlatiladi; that ishlatilmaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat mos olmoshni yozing: Our new scanner, ___ arrived on Tuesday, is already in use. (which / that)
questions.explanation: Non-defining relative gapda narsa uchun which kerak. That vergul bilan ajratilgan bunday gapga mos emas.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Qo‘shimcha ma’lumot: My laptop, ___ is six years old, still works. (which / that)
questions.explanation: Non-defining gapda buyum uchun which ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: That o‘rniga odamga mos olmosh: Mr Lee, that lives upstairs, is a pilot.
expected: Mr Lee, who lives upstairs, is a pilot.
questions.explanation: Vergulli qo‘shimcha ma’lumotda who kerak.

questions.prompt: Which bilan qo‘shing; is electric bilan tugating, nisbiy qismni vergullar bilan ajrating: Our car is electric. It was made in Korea.
expected: Our car, which was made in Korea, is electric.
questions.explanation: Qo‘shimcha ma’lumot which bilan va ikki vergul orasida keladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Non-defining gapda which ni tushirish mumkinmi? A) Ha, har doim. B) Yo‘q.
questions.explanation: Qo‘shimcha nisbiy gapning olmoshi saqlanadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat mos so‘zni yozing: Elena, ___ daughter is a violinist, invited us to a concert. (whose / who)
questions.explanation: Daughter oldidan egalikni bildiruvchi whose ishlatiladi. Bu qo‘shimcha ma’lumotli gaplarda ham mumkin.

questions.prompt: Faqat mos so‘zni yozing: Lisbon, ___ we spent our honeymoon, has steep streets. (where / which)
questions.explanation: Ergash gapda Lisbon harakat sodir bo‘lgan joy. Where bu yerda in which ma’nosini beradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Qo‘shimcha egalik: Mr Karimov, ___ son won a scholarship, is delighted.
questions.explanation: Whose qo‘shimcha qismda ham egalikni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Joy ravishi: Samarkand, which my cousin lives, attracts many visitors. Where ishlating.
expected: Samarkand, where my cousin lives, attracts many visitors.
questions.explanation: Where my cousin lives joydagi holatni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Whose bilan qo‘shing; is a designer bilan tugating, vergullar qo‘ying: Amina is a designer. Her brother is a chef.
expected: Amina, whose brother is a chef, is a designer.
questions.explanation: Her brother → whose brother qo‘shimcha ma’lumotga aylanadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “Oxford, where I studied, is busy in summer” gapida where qismi: A) Qo‘shimcha ma’lumot. B) Qaysi Oxford ekanini zarur ajratish.
questions.explanation: Vergullar qo‘shimcha ma’lumotni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Bir nechta ammam bor; faqat shifokor bo‘lganini ajratmoqchiman. A) My aunt who is a doctor works nights. B) My aunt, who is a doctor, works nights.
questions.explanation: Qaysi amma ekanini aniqlash uchun who is a doctor zarur. Defining relative gap vergulsiz yoziladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Bitta velosipedim bor; rangini qo‘shimcha ma’lumot sifatida aytaman. A) My bicycle which is yellow needs new tyres. B) My bicycle, which is yellow, needs new tyres.
questions.explanation: Velosiped allaqachon aniq, rang esa qo‘shimcha ma’lumot. Non-defining gap ikki tomondan vergul bilan ajratiladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Faqat ko‘k nishonli ishchilar kirishi mumkin. A) Workers who have blue badges may enter. B) Workers, who have blue badges, may enter.
questions.explanation: Vergulsiz nisbiy qism kerakli guruhni ajratadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “My sons, who live abroad, visit each summer” nimani anglatadi? A) Faqat ayrim o‘g‘illarim chet elda. B) Gapdagi barcha o‘g‘illarim chet elda.
questions.explanation: Vergulli qism tilga olingan barcha o‘g‘illarga qo‘shimcha ma’lumot beradi.

questions.prompt: Qo‘shimcha ma’lumotni alohida gap qiling: My sister, who studies medicine, is twenty. Avval yoshini, keyin She bilan o‘qishini ayting.
expected: My sister is twenty. She studies medicine.
questions.explanation: Qo‘shimcha nisbiy qismni ajratsak, asosiy ma’no saqlanadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Standart yozuvda qo‘shimcha qismni to‘g‘ri ajrating: A) Our coach, who is very patient, helped us. B) Our coach, who is very patient helped us.
questions.explanation: Gap o‘rtasidagi qo‘shimcha qism ikki tomondan ajratiladi.

questions.prompt: Rasmiy uslubdagi mos olmoshni yozing: The consultant with ___ we negotiated was patient. (whom / that)
questions.explanation: Oldinga chiqarilgan predlogdan keyin odam uchun whom ishlatiladi: with whom. With that bu nisbiy tuzilmada mumkin emas.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Nisbiy gapning oddiy va rasmiy shakllari qaysi juftlikda to‘g‘ri? A) the grant I applied for / the grant for which I applied B) the grant I applied for / the grant for that I applied
questions.explanation: Oddiy uslubda predlog oxirda qolishi mumkin. Rasmiy shaklda predlog oldinga chiqsa, narsa uchun which kerak, that emas.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Rasmiy nisbiy gap: The organisation for ___ she works is expanding.
questions.explanation: Predlogdan keyin buyum/tashkilot uchun which keladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Predlogdan keyingi olmosh: The researcher to that I wrote replied.
expected: The researcher to whom I wrote replied.
questions.explanation: Odamga oid predlogdan keyin whom ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Rasmiy to whom qolipiga o‘tkazing: The woman I spoke to was the director.
expected: The woman to whom I spoke was the director.
questions.explanation: Predlogni boshga ko‘chirganda whom saqlanadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Qaysi shakl odatiy suhbat uslubida? A) the colleague with whom I travelled B) the colleague I travelled with
questions.explanation: Suhbatda predlog ko‘pincha nisbiy qism oxirida qoladi.

questions.prompt: Butun oldingi fikrga ishora qiluvchi olmoshni tanlang: The team finished two days early, ___ surprised the client. (which / what)
questions.explanation: Which bu yerda bitta otga emas, jamoaning ikki kun oldin tugatganiga ishora qiladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. ‘The bus never arrived, which made us late.’ gapida which nimaga ishora qiladi? A) Avtobusning kelmaganiga. B) Faqat bus otiga.
questions.explanation: Kechikishga avtobusning kelmagani sabab bo‘lgan. Which oldingi gapdagi butun vaziyatni anglatadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Butun fikrga ishora: Nobody objected, ___ surprised the chairperson.
questions.explanation: Which oldingi butun voqeaga ishora qiladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Butun gapga ishora: She remembered my birthday, what was thoughtful.
expected: She remembered my birthday, which was thoughtful.
questions.explanation: Oldingi fikrga which ishlatiladi, what emas.

questions.prompt: Which bilan birlashtiring: He paid for everyone's lunch. This was generous.
expected: He paid for everyone's lunch, which was generous.
questions.explanation: Which uning hamma uchun to‘laganiga ishora qiladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “The lift broke down, which delayed us” gapida which nimaga ishora qiladi? A) Liftning buzilganiga. B) Faqat liftning rangiga.
questions.explanation: Which oldingi butun holatni bog‘laydi.

questions.prompt: Who is qismini tushirib, fe’lni -ing shaklida saqlang. Butun gapni yozing: The technician who is testing the alarm needs silence.
expected: The technician testing the alarm needs silence.
questions.explanation: Faol davomiy harakatni ifodalovchi who is testing qisqartirilganda testing qoladi.

questions.prompt: Qisqartirilgan faol aniqlovchi uchun fe’l shaklini yozing: Passengers ___ to Rome should go to gate twelve. (travel)
questions.explanation: Yo‘lovchilar harakatni bajaradi, shuning uchun -ing shakli kerak. Travelling Britaniya, traveling Amerika imlosi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Qisqa faol aniqlovchi: Anyone ___ (wish) to join should email us.
questions.explanation: Faol aniqlovchida -ing ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Qisqartirilgan faol qism: The girl stand by the window is my cousin.
expected: The girl standing by the window is my cousin.
questions.explanation: Girl bajaruvchi; standing bilan aniqlanadi.

questions.prompt: Who are ni tushiring: The people who are queuing outside need tickets.
expected: The people queuing outside need tickets.
questions.explanation: Who are queuing → queuing.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “The train approaching platform two” ma’nosi: A) Ikkinchi yo‘lakka yaqinlashayotgan poyezd. B) Ikkinchi yo‘lakda ta’mirlangan poyezd.
questions.explanation: Approaching faol jarayonni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Which were qismini olib tashlab, butun gapni yozing: The samples which were collected yesterday are frozen.
expected: The samples collected yesterday are frozen.
questions.explanation: Passiv aniqlovchi qisqartirilganda V3 qoladi: collected. Namunalar harakatni bajarmaydi, ular yig‘ilgan.

questions.prompt: Qisqartirilgan passiv aniqlovchidagi fe’l shaklini yozing: The jewellery ___ from the gallery has been recovered. (steal)
questions.explanation: Zargarlik buyumlari o‘g‘irlangan, shuning uchun steal ning V3 shakli stolen kerak; stealing faol ma’no beradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Qisqa passiv aniqlovchi: The goods ___ (damage) in transit will be replaced.
questions.explanation: Goods ish ta’sirida; V3 damaged ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Qisqa passiv: The messages sending yesterday were confidential. V3 ishlating.
expected: The messages sent yesterday were confidential.
questions.explanation: Xabarlar yuborilgan; sent passiv ma’no beradi.

questions.prompt: That was ni tushiring: The bridge that was built in 1880 is still in use.
expected: The bridge built in 1880 is still in use.
questions.explanation: That was built → built qisqa passivdir.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “The forms signed by the manager” ma’nosi: A) Menejerga imzo qo‘ygan blankalar. B) Menejer imzolagan blankalar.
questions.explanation: Signed V3 blankalarga bajarilgan ishni bildiradi.

sections.title: Week 23 · The Bench Visitors Could Find
sections.text: A park survey asked visitors which benches they liked. Most responses praised a new wooden bench beside the pond. The council planned to copy it throughout the park. Then an access volunteer, whose group had not received the survey, pointed out that the path to that bench was too narrow for some mobility aids. People who could not reach it were unlikely to evaluate it. The council invited another group, including residents who usually entered through the north gate, to walk the proposed sites. sections.text: Our photography club decided to redesign its beginner workshop after several learners avoided returning for a second session. They enjoyed taking pictures but disliked spending most of the evening watching slides. The tutor had hoped to explain every camera setting before allowing practice. sections.text: Reading the instructions for our booking form took longer than completing the form itself. The guide was accurate, but it was too dense to use quickly at the reception desk. Important warnings sat between background explanations and technical definitions. We tested a shorter version with new volunteers. Finding the next step became easier, although some unusual cases still required the full guide. The solution was not to delete complexity entirely. We created a short action sheet and linked each section to the detailed reference. Using plain language helped people notice the exceptions instead of hiding them in a wall of text. The new sheet was clear enough to support routine tasks, but not broad enough to answer every possible question. That limit was stated at the top. Good instructions do not promise to remove all judgement. They make ordinary decisions easier and show users when to seek help. Our reception desk now has fewer pages and fewer panicked whispers.

sections.text: I used to drive to the training centre, but the new parking fee encouraged me to try taking the bus. At first, I was not used to waiting outside in bad weather. I tried to read on the journey, but motion made that uncomfortable, so I tried listening to short audio lessons instead. That worked better. One morning, I stopped to buy a ticket and forgot to collect the receipt I needed for reimbursement. I remember telling the driver about my course, but not checking the machine. Now I set a reminder to keep the receipt. The change has not made every journey pleasant. Some buses are crowded, and the evening connection is unreliable. Still, I have stopped assuming that driving is always the only practical choice. A trial should allow mixed results. Otherwise, one wet morning becomes proof against buses, while years of traffic delays somehow count as normal life.

sections.text: Our charity recently moved into a shared office, and we are getting used to working beside two other teams. At first, small habits caused surprising tension. We turned the heating up while our neighbours opened a window. We depended on informal messages, but nobody knew who was responsible for locking up. After a meeting, we wrote a short agreement and had the faulty door lock replaced. We also got the meeting-room screen repaired instead of asking volunteers to fix it without training. The agreement includes turning lights off, looking after shared equipment and checking with other teams before moving furniture. These rules are not a substitute for courtesy, but they reduce repeated uncertainty. I am interested in how quickly trust improves when responsibilities become visible. A shared office does not require everyone to work in the same way. It requires people to notice where one team's convenient habit becomes another team's daily problem.

sections.text: Our community workshop wants to attract new members without overwhelming them. We used to begin with a long tour and ask everyone to remember every rule immediately. Several newcomers admitted feeling lost, although they appreciated the volunteers' friendliness. We decided to try offering a short welcome task instead. A trained member helps each person to label a sample item, find the correct storage place and practise recording a loan. Doing one complete task makes the wider system easier to understand. We still expect people to read the safety information, and they must not use unfamiliar equipment without guidance. The team also had damaged signs replaced and is getting used to explaining fewer details at once. Some experienced members worry that the new approach is too simple. We will therefore review errors and newcomer feedback after four sessions. The aim is not to remove standards. It is to help people reach them through a sequence they can actually follow.

sections.transcript:
Director: Why do you recommend changing the induction session?
Coordinator: New volunteers enjoy helping people, but they struggle to remember twenty procedures before trying any of them. I suggest starting with one supervised task.
Director: Would that be enough to prepare them?
Coordinator: Enough for a first step, not for independent work. We would still require them to read the safety guide and ask before using unfamiliar equipment.
Director: What else needs attention?
Coordinator: We should have the unclear signs replaced. We also need to stop assuming that silence means understanding.
Director: How will you check the new approach?
Coordinator: By observing errors, listening to feedback and asking volunteers to explain the next step in their own words.
Director: Good. Please send a written proposal with a four-session review point. A simpler beginning is useful if it leads to stronger understanding, not if it merely makes the timetable look less demanding.

expected:
Dear Ms Rahim,
I am writing to propose a revised introduction for new workshop volunteers. Several newcomers have admitted feeling overwhelmed by the number of procedures presented before they can practise anything.
I suggest beginning with one supervised task: labelling an item, finding its storage place and recording a loan. Completing this sequence should make the system easier to understand. Volunteers would still be required to read the safety guide and ask before using unfamiliar equipment.
We should also have the unclear signs replaced and stop treating silence as evidence of understanding. Could you approve a four-session trial of this approach? We would review errors, collect feedback and ask participants to explain the next step in their own words.
Please let me know whether the trial can begin next month and who should coordinate the review.
Yours sincerely,
Malika Saidova

Muammo, usul, ruxsat va baholash bandlari to‘liq.
Fe’l qoliplari va causative ma’noga mos.

sections.title: Week 24 · Keeping New Members
sections.text: Our chess club enjoys welcoming new players, but many leave after their first evening. The committee considered reducing the membership price. A volunteer suggested asking recent visitors about their experience before deciding. Several reported feeling lost because regular members began games immediately and expected newcomers to understand the pairing board. They did not mention the price. The committee agreed to try a welcome table and asked two experienced players to explain the system. Members who prefer starting immediately can still do so. The club also stopped describing the beginner session as a tournament, since that word made some visitors expect formal competition. Next month the committee plans to compare return visits and collect short comments. It hopes to make participation easier without promising that every visitor will become a regular member.

A neighbourhood pool introduced discounted lunchtime entry for six weeks. Attendance rose by a third, so its first report called the scheme a clear success. Although more people entered the building, ticket income fell slightly. The report also omitted whether the new visitors were previously inactive or simply changed the time of their usual swim.

If the aim was to reduce crowding in the evening, the relevant evidence is evening occupancy, not merely lunchtime attendance.
Despite these gaps, the experiment produced one useful finding. Several nearby office workers formed a regular swimming group and reported that a fixed meeting time helped them continue. Their comments suggest a social benefit, though a small group cannot speak for everyone.
The next report should therefore compare attendance across the whole day and include staff costs. It should also ask occasional users why they stopped coming. An attractive photograph of a busy pool is encouraging; however, a photograph cannot show who stayed away or whether the improvement lasted after the discount ended.

Manager: Our new kiosk has reduced the average check-in time, so I want to remove the old reception desk.
Receptionist: Although most guests finish quickly, some need help with names, languages or access requests. Their waiting time has increased because one employee now handles every difficult case.
Manager: The average still improved by three minutes.
Receptionist: Yes, but an average can hide very different experiences. A guest who finishes in thirty seconds and another who waits fifteen minutes do not receive the same service.
Manager: Would keeping both systems defeat the purpose of automation?
Receptionist: Not necessarily. Despite the kiosk's speed, we still need a visible route to personal assistance. We could reduce the desk rather than remove it.
Manager: That would preserve part of the staffing cost.
Receptionist: It would. However, repeated complaints also consume staff time. Yesterday I explained the same error to six guests because nobody had updated the on-screen instructions.
Manager: Then let's improve those instructions and measure assisted check-ins separately.

sections.text:
Two neighbourhoods have chosen different ways to make household tools affordable. One runs a lending library, whereas the other negotiates discounts at a hardware shop. The library spreads the cost of rarely used items across many borrowers. The discount scheme gives people permanent access, but each household still needs storage and maintenance.
Supporters of lending point to a carpet cleaner that was borrowed thirty times in one year. It was such a popular item that the library bought a second machine. Yet not every tool circulates so well. An unusually heavy drill remained on its shelf because beginners found it intimidating. The collection therefore needs regular review rather than endless expansion.
The shop scheme is simpler to administer. Customers choose their own products, while volunteers only arrange the discount. However, a cheaper purchase can still be unnecessary. One resident admitted that his bargain drill had spent longer in its attractive box than outside it.
Neither approach is automatically more responsible. Lending works best when collection times, training and repairs are reliable. Discounts are more suitable for equipment people use frequently. The sensible question is not which scheme sounds more generous, but which one matches actual patterns of use and the capacity of local volunteers.

sections.text:
The organisers of a neighbourhood market have ordered removable covers in order to keep the event outdoors during light rain. They will not cancel merely because the forecast mentions showers. Instead, they have agreed on clear conditions for moving indoors, including strong wind and standing water near electrical equipment.
Volunteers will inspect the site before stalls open. They will keep a paper list of sellers in case the mobile connection fails, and they will call each seller if the venue changes. The distinction matters: a backup is prepared beforehand, whereas a call follows a specific decision.
Some traders argue that preparation creates unnecessary expense. Their concern is understandable after two completely dry years. However, the covers can be reused, and the alternative indoor space requires an advance reservation anyway. Waiting until the first storm would leave everyone competing for the same limited room.
The team also plans signs so that visitors can find the indoor entrance without asking at every stall. As soon as a move is confirmed, one volunteer will update the website while another checks the street signs. The plan does not eliminate bad weather; it prevents ordinary uncertainty from turning into several contradictory announcements delivered through increasingly wet phones.

sections.text:
A volunteer repair cafe advertises both practical assistance and opportunities to learn. Visitors can either leave a simple item with a volunteer or remain at the table and observe the process. Neither option guarantees a successful repair, and the organisers state that clearly on the booking form.
The learning element is not only a pleasant extra but also a possible way to reduce future waste. For example, a visitor who learns to clean a blocked filter may avoid replacing an appliance unnecessarily. Nevertheless, the cafe does not record such later decisions, so it cannot claim to have measured every environmental benefit.
Its strongest evidence is modest and specific: during the last session, volunteers restored eighteen of twenty-seven items. Four needed unavailable parts, while five were unsafe or beyond the team's expertise. Publishing those categories builds more trust than announcing that the event 'saved everything'.
Some residents would prefer a paid repair service with a fixed deadline. That is a reasonable alternative, especially for essential equipment. Moreover, volunteers should not be expected to replace professional services for every household. The cafe's value lies in extending options, sharing knowledge and directing difficult cases elsewhere. A successful community project can acknowledge its limits without turning its publicity into an apology.

Director: We can either offer a low fixed price or introduce a voluntary contribution. Both approaches are more accessible than our current ticket.
Treasurer: A voluntary contribution may work, but income would be less predictable. Neither goodwill nor a busy entrance automatically pays for maintenance.
Director: True. It could attract people who assume the museum is beyond their budget.
Treasurer: Then we should test that claim. For instance, ask visitors whether price influenced their decision, without making them justify their finances at the desk.
Director: I like that. The change should not only increase attendance but also make people feel welcome.
Treasurer: And we need clear wording. 'Free entry, suggested contribution' means something different from a compulsory charge with a friendly name.
Director: Some donors might compensate for lower payments.
Treasurer: They might; however, we should not build the entire budget on that hope. Keep a reserve and review income monthly.
Director: So a three-month pilot, private optional feedback and a visible explanation of where donations go?
Treasurer: Yes. I support a carefully measured experiment. I simply want the museum to remain open after the enthusiastic launch photographs have disappeared from everyone's feed.
Director: Fair enough. Our announcement can describe the opportunity and the uncertainty together.

sections.text:
The town's first car-free Sunday drew a large crowd into the central square. Cafes reported strong sales, while a furniture shop said customers could not collect bulky purchases. Both reports may be accurate because businesses use the same street in different ways. A single total for visitor numbers would miss that distinction.
The organisers closed the road in order to create space for walking and public activities. They also provided a delivery window before nine. However, the notice reached some traders only two days beforehand, so several existing collections could not easily be rearranged. Better communication would address that problem without necessarily abandoning the event.
Residents raised a different concern: traffic moved into neighbouring streets. Although the square was quieter, those households experienced more noise. The next trial should therefore monitor surrounding roads as well as the closed area. Otherwise, an improvement in one visible location may simply transfer inconvenience elsewhere.
A second event is justified if organisers use the first as evidence rather than as a celebration that cannot be questioned. They should publish both gains and costs, consult people beyond the square, and announce arrangements early. Success means a workable balance of access and public space, not merely a photograph with fewer cars.

sections.transcript:
Team Lead: Our shared-desk trial has reduced unused office space, but the feedback is mixed. We need a recommendation for the next quarter.
Analyst: The savings are clear. However, staff who need specialised equipment spend time rebuilding their workspace each morning.
Team Lead: Could we reserve a few permanent stations so that those tasks remain efficient?
Analyst: Yes. Either a fixed station or a reliable equipment locker could help, depending on the role. We should ask about tasks rather than rank people by seniority.
Team Lead: Some colleagues say fixed desks would undermine fairness.
Analyst: Equal furniture is not always equal access. A worker using two calibrated monitors has a different requirement from someone mainly attending meetings.
Team Lead: What about social contact? The trial was supposed to encourage new conversations.
Analyst: We have comments about that, but no consistent evidence. People may meet different colleagues while also losing contact with their immediate team.
Team Lead: Then we should retain the trial and revise its rules?
Analyst: For another month, yes, provided we measure setup time and missed collaboration as well as space savings. Keep spare stations in case bookings fail. The system should support work, not turn finding a chair into everyone's first project of the day.
Team Lead: I'll present that as a conditional recommendation.

I would support another car-free Sunday, but not a monthly commitment yet. The first event showed that the square can become an attractive public space. It also revealed problems that deserve more than a photograph.
Cafes benefited from visitors, whereas a furniture shop struggled with collections. These experiences do not cancel each other out. They show why organisers need to consider different kinds of business. An early delivery window is useful, but traders must receive enough notice to rearrange existing appointments.
The traffic in neighbouring streets is an important issue. A quieter square is not a complete success if nearby households receive all the displaced noise. The next trial should count traffic around the area as well as inside it and invite comments from those residents.
Some supporters may worry that further checks will delay a popular idea. I understand that concern, yet a short evaluation could prevent repeated mistakes and strengthen support. Announce the next date early, publish the delivery arrangements, and compare benefits with inconvenience afterwards. If the revised event improves access without simply moving problems elsewhere, a regular programme would have a stronger case. Public enthusiasm is valuable, but practical evidence should shape the final timetable.

questions.explanation: Since you’re here kelib turganingiz sababini bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat mos iborani yozing: The museum closed early ___ a power failure. (because / because of)
questions.explanation: A power failure ot birikmasi, shu sababli uning oldidan because of ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat mos iborani yozing: Several trains were delayed ___ heavy snowfall. (due to / since)
questions.explanation: Heavy snowfall ot birikmasi. Due to + ot birikmasi sababni bildiradi; sabab bildiruvchi since esa ega-fe’lli gap bilan keladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Ot birikmasi: The event was moved indoors ___ the strong wind. (because / because of)
questions.explanation: Because of dan keyin ot birikmasi keladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Due to qolipi: The delay was due the strike.
expected: The delay was due to the strike.
questions.explanation: Due to to‘liq birikma bo‘lishi kerak.

questions.prompt: Because of bilan yozing: The path was closed because there was a landslide. The path bilan boshlang.
expected: The path was closed because of a landslide.
questions.explanation: Because + gap o‘rniga because of + ot keladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. To‘g‘ri birikma: A) due to poor visibility B) due to it was foggy
questions.explanation: Due to odatda ot yoki ot birikmasini oladi.

questions.prompt: Natijani bildiruvchi bog‘lovchini tanlang: The battery was flat, ___ the car would not start. (so / because) Faqat so‘zni yozing.
questions.explanation: Birinchi qism sabab, ikkinchisi natija. So avtomobilning yurmaganini natija sifatida bog‘laydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat mos iborani yozing: The factory installed better filters. ___, the air nearby became cleaner. (As a result / For example)
questions.explanation: Havoning tozalanishi filtrlar o‘rnatilishining natijasi. As a result shu natijani ko‘rsatadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Natija: The water supply was cut off, ___ we bought bottled water. (so / because)
questions.explanation: So sababdan keyin natijani kiritadi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Bog‘lanish ma’nosi: The key broke, because we couldn't open the door. Because o‘rniga so ishlating.
expected: The key broke, so we couldn't open the door.
The key broke, so we could not open the door.
questions.explanation: Ocholmaslik kalit sinishining natijasidir.

questions.prompt: Therefore bilan ulang, nuqtali vergul ishlating: The evidence was weak. The case was dismissed.
expected: The evidence was weak; therefore, the case was dismissed.
questions.explanation: Therefore natija bildiradi; mustaqil gaplar nuqtali vergul bilan ajraladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “The roads froze. As a result, several schools closed.” Yopilish: A) Sabab. B) Natija.
questions.explanation: As a result oqibatni kiritadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat mos bog‘lovchini yozing: ___ the route was steep, the children reached the top. (Although / Despite)
questions.explanation: The route was steep ega-fe’lli gap. Although undan oldin kelib, kutilmagan qarama-qarshilikni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. To‘g‘ri gapni tanlang: A) Even though the shop was busy, but the assistant remained calm. B) Even though the shop was busy, the assistant remained calm.
questions.explanation: Even though bilan boshlangan zidlov ergash gapdan keyin shu vazifa uchun yana but qo‘shilmaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Zidlik + gap: ___ she was nervous, she gave a clear presentation. (Although / Despite)
questions.explanation: Although dan keyin to‘liq gap keladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Ortiqcha but ni olib tashlang: Although the queue was long, but we waited.
expected: Although the queue was long, we waited.
questions.explanation: Although va but bitta juft gapda birga kerak emas.

questions.prompt: Even though bilan boshlang: The tickets cost a lot. We bought them.
expected: Even though the tickets cost a lot, we bought them.
questions.explanation: Even though kutilmagan zid natijani kuchliroq ta’kidlaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “Although he apologised, she remained upset” ma’nosi: A) Uzr so‘ragani uchun xafa bo‘ldi. B) Uzr so‘ragan bo‘lsa ham xafaligi qolgan.
questions.explanation: Although yon berish va zidlikni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat fe’l shaklini yozing: Despite ___ a headache, Karim finished the rehearsal. (have)
questions.explanation: Despite dan keyin ot yoki -ing shakli keladi: despite having a headache.

questions.prompt: Faqat yetishmayotgan bitta so‘zni yozing: In spite ___ the noise, the baby stayed asleep.
questions.explanation: To‘liq birikma in spite of. Undan keyin the noise kabi ot birikmasi kelishi mumkin.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Despite + -ing: Despite ___ (feel) unwell, she attended the briefing.
questions.explanation: Despite dan keyin ot yoki -ing keladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Ortiqcha predlog: Despite of the heat, they kept working.
expected: Despite the heat, they kept working.
questions.explanation: Despite dan keyin of ishlatilmaydi.

questions.prompt: In spite of bilan yozing: Although he was tired, he finished the race. Being ishlating.
expected: In spite of being tired, he finished the race.
questions.explanation: In spite of dan keyin being tired otlashgan qismdir.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. To‘g‘ri gap: A) Despite the heavy traffic, we arrived early. B) Despite the traffic was heavy, we arrived early.
questions.explanation: Despite to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri to‘liq gapni olmaydi.

questions.prompt: Qarama-qarshi fikrni bog‘lang; faqat mos so‘zni yozing: The tickets were expensive. ___, every seat was sold. (Nevertheless / Therefore)
questions.explanation: Qimmatlikka qaramay hamma joy sotilgan. Nevertheless kutilmagan zid natijani bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat mos so‘zni yozing: The instructions looked simple. ___, assembling the desk took hours. (However / Moreover)
questions.explanation: Oddiy ko‘ringan yo‘riqnoma bilan uzoq davom etgan yig‘ish jarayoni zid. However qarama-qarshi fikrni kiritadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Qarshi fikr: The task looked impossible. ___, they completed it. (Nevertheless / Therefore)
questions.explanation: Nevertheless kutilgan natijaga qarshi fikrni kiritadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Standart tinish belgisi: A) It was costly, however, we agreed. B) It was costly; however, we agreed.
questions.explanation: However ikki mustaqil gapni faqat vergul bilan bog‘lamaydi.

questions.prompt: But o‘rniga However ishlating; ikkita gap yozing: The room was small, but it was comfortable.
expected: The room was small. However, it was comfortable.
questions.explanation: However yangi gapdagi qarshi fikrni kiritadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “He lacked experience. Nevertheless, he succeeded.” ma’nosi: A) Tajribasi kam bo‘lsa ham muvaffaqiyatga erishdi. B) Tajribasi ko‘pligi sabab muvaffaqiyatga erishdi.
questions.explanation: Nevertheless to‘siqqa qaramay natijani bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Ikki kishining qarama-qarshi odatini bog‘lang: I save every receipt, ___ my brother throws them away. (whereas / because) Faqat so‘zni yozing.
questions.explanation: Whereas ikki turli odatni taqqoslab, qarama-qarshi qo‘yadi; sabab bildirmaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Qaysi gapda while vaqtni emas, qarama-qarshilikni bildiradi? A) While I was washing up, the phone rang. B) The north is dry, while the south is humid.
questions.explanation: B gapida while ikki hududning iqlimini taqqoslaydi. A gapida esa hodisa qachon bo‘lganini ko‘rsatadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Taqqoslash: This model is light, ___ the older one is heavy. (whereas / because)
questions.explanation: Whereas ikki modelning farqini ko‘rsatadi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Qarama-qarshi taqqoslashda because ni whereas ga almashtiring: I prefer working alone, because she prefers teamwork.
expected: I prefer working alone, whereas she prefers teamwork.
questions.explanation: Whereas sabab emas, farqni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: While bilan birlashtiring; The north bilan boshlang: The north gets snow. The south stays warm.
expected: The north gets snow, while the south stays warm.
questions.explanation: While bu yerda ikki hududni qarama-qarshi qo‘yadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Qaysi while taqqoslashni bildiradi? A) I fell while I was skiing. B) Ben cycles, while Anna takes the bus.
questions.explanation: Ikki kishining odati solishtirilmoqda.

questions.prompt: Faqat mos so‘zni yozing: The tunnel was ___ narrow that two cars could not pass. (so / such)
questions.explanation: Narrow sifatidan oldin so ishlatiladi: so + sifat + that + natija.

questions.prompt: Faqat mos so‘zni yozing: The actor spoke ___ softly that we could barely hear him. (so / such)
questions.explanation: Softly ravish; so + ravish + that qolipi uning darajasi keltirib chiqargan natijani bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Sifat + natija: The instructions were ___ unclear that we called for help.
questions.explanation: So + sifat + that natijani beradi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Ravish kuchaytirgichi: She ran such fast that nobody caught her.
expected: She ran so fast that nobody caught her.
questions.explanation: Ravish fast oldidan so keladi.

questions.prompt: So…that bilan birlashtiring: The box was very heavy. We needed a trolley.
expected: The box was so heavy that we needed a trolley.
questions.explanation: So heavy daraja sababli natijani bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “He spoke so quietly that I missed his name” gapida I missed his name: A) Natija. B) Maqsad.
questions.explanation: So…that maqsad emas, daraja natijasidir.

questions.prompt: Faqat mos so‘zni yozing: It was ___ an exciting final that nobody left early. (so / such)
questions.explanation: An exciting final ot birikmasi. Such + a/an + sifat + ot + that qolipi ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat mos so‘zni yozing: They gave us ___ useful directions that we found the cabin immediately. (so / such)
questions.explanation: Useful directions sifat va ko‘plikdagi otdan iborat. Such qo‘llanadi, ammo ko‘plik ot oldidan a/an kelmaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Ot birikmasi: It was ___ a windy day that the ferry stayed in port.
questions.explanation: Such a + sifat + birlik ot + that.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Artikl: It was such useful tool that everyone wanted one.
expected: It was such a useful tool that everyone wanted one.
questions.explanation: Birlik sanaladigan tool oldidan a kerak.

questions.prompt: Such…that bilan qayta yozing: The music was so loud that we couldn't talk. It was bilan boshlang.
expected: It was such loud music that we couldn't talk.
It was such loud music that we could not talk.
questions.explanation: Music sanalmaydi; such loud music, artiklsiz.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. To‘g‘ri gap: A) They were such a friendly people. B) They were such friendly people.
questions.explanation: Ko‘plik people oldidan a qo‘yilmaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat yetishmayotgan so‘zni yozing: We left quietly in order ___ wake the patients. (not to / to not to)
questions.explanation: Inkor maqsad in order not to + fe’l bilan beriladi: bemorlarni uyg‘otmaslik uchun.

questions.prompt: Faqat kerakli so‘zni yozing: The archivist wore gloves so as ___ protect the old letters. (to / for)
questions.explanation: Maqsad bildiruvchi to‘liq birikma so as to. Undan keyin protect asosiy shaklda keladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Maqsad: She labelled every box in order ___ confusion. (avoid)
questions.explanation: In order to + asosiy fe’l maqsad bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Maqsad qolipi: We whispered so as not wake the baby.
expected: We whispered so as not to wake the baby.
questions.explanation: Inkor maqsad so as not to + fe’l.

questions.prompt: In order to bilan birlashtiring: I took notes. I wanted to remember the details.
expected: I took notes in order to remember the details.
questions.explanation: Infinitiv bir xil eganing maqsadini ko‘rsatadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “They left early so as to avoid the crowds” ma’nosi: A) Gavjumlikdan qochish uchun erta ketishdi. B) Erta ketgani uchun olomon paydo bo‘ldi.
questions.explanation: So as to maqsadni ifodalaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat mos iborani yozing: I emailed the diagram ___ the engineer could check it before the meeting. (so that / in order to)
questions.explanation: Keyingi qismning o‘z egasi va modal fe’li bor: the engineer could. Bunday maqsad gapini so that bog‘laydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Grammatik jihatdan to‘g‘ri maqsad gapini tanlang: A) We lowered the shelf so that the children could reach it. B) We lowered the shelf so that the children to reach it.
questions.explanation: So that dan keyin ega va tuslangan fe’l kerak. Could reach shu vazifani bajaradi; to reach mustaqil kesim emas.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Maqsad + ega-fe’l: We drew a map ___ visitors could find the hall.
questions.explanation: So that dan keyin to‘liq gap keladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Maqsad gapi: She moved aside so that I to see the board. Could ishlating.
expected: She moved aside so that I could see the board.
questions.explanation: So that + ega + could + fe’l kerak.

questions.prompt: So that bilan birlashtiring: I enlarged the text. I wanted my grandfather to be able to read it. Could ishlating.
expected: I enlarged the text so that my grandfather could read it.
questions.explanation: Ikki xil ega maqsad gapida so that bilan bog‘lanadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “Speak clearly so that everyone can hear” ma’nosi: A) Hamma allaqachon eshitgani uchun. B) Hamma eshita olishi uchun.
questions.explanation: So that bu gapda maqsadni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Kelajak haqida gap: faqat to‘g‘ri fe’l shaklini yozing: I will message you as soon as the plane ___. (lands / will land)
questions.explanation: Kelajak ma’nosidagi as soon as vaqt ergash gapida odatda Present Simple ishlatiladi, will qo‘yilmaydi.

questions.prompt: Kutishning tugash chegarasini ko‘rsating; faqat bog‘lovchini yozing: Do not unplug the device ___ the update is complete. (until / after)
questions.explanation: Not ... until yangilanish tugamaguncha qurilmani uzmaslikni bildiradi. Until kutilayotgan chegara vaqtini belgilaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Kelajak vaqt qismi: We will begin after everyone ___ (arrive).
questions.explanation: After vaqt qismida kelajak uchun Present Simple keladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Vaqt qismi: I will unlock the door before you will arrive.
expected: I will unlock the door before you arrive.
I'll unlock the door before you arrive.
questions.explanation: Before dan keyin oddiy kelajak ma’nosida will kerak emas.

questions.prompt: As soon as bilan boshlang: The lights come on. We will enter immediately.
expected: As soon as the lights come on, we will enter.
As soon as the lights come on, we'll enter.
questions.explanation: As soon as darhol keyingi harakatni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “Stay here until I call” ma’nosi: A) Qo‘ng‘iroq qilgunimcha shu yerda qoling. B) Qo‘ng‘iroq qilganimdan keyin keling.
questions.explanation: Until harakat davom etadigan chegarani bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Oldindan ehtiyot chorasi nazarda tutilgan. Faqat iborani yozing: Save an offline copy ___ the internet fails during the presentation. (in case / if)
questions.explanation: In case ehtimoliy muammo yuz berishidan oldin tayyorlanishni bildiradi: internet uzilib qolishi ehtimoliga qarshi nusxa saqlanadi.

questions.prompt: Yordamni faqat muammo yuz bergandagina chaqiring. Faqat bog‘lovchini yozing: Call the technician ___ the screen goes black. (if / in case)
questions.explanation: If shartni bildiradi: ekran o‘chsa, shundan keyin texnik chaqiriladi. Bu oldindan ehtiyot chorasi emas.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Oldindan ehtiyot chorasi: Bring a spare shirt ___ this one gets wet. (in case / if)
questions.explanation: In case ehtimoliy muammo uchun tayyorgarlikdir.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Ehtiyot gapidagi zamon: Take some cash in case the card machine will fail.
expected: Take some cash in case the card machine fails.
questions.explanation: In case dan keyin kelajak uchun Present Simple kerak.

questions.prompt: In case bilan birlashtiring: I wrote down the address. I was afraid I might forget it.
expected: I wrote down the address in case I forgot it.
questions.explanation: Oldingi ehtiyot chorasi uchun in case + past ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “Use the spare key if you lose yours” ma’nosi: A) Hozirning o‘zida zaxira kalitni ishlating. B) Faqat kalitingizni yo‘qotsangiz, zaxirasini ishlating.
questions.explanation: If chorani shart yuz bergandan keyinga bog‘laydi.

questions.prompt: Ikkalasida ham yo‘qligini bildiring; faqat bog‘lovchini yozing: Neither the cabin ___ the tent has electricity. (or / nor)
questions.explanation: Neither ... nor juftligi ikki narsani ham inkor qiladi. Neither bilan nor moslashadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Qaysi variantda ikkala juft bog‘lovchi to‘g‘ri? A) Both tea or juice are available; choose either tea and juice. B) Both tea and juice are available; choose either tea or juice.
questions.explanation: Both ... and ikkalasini qo‘shadi. Either ... or esa ikkita variantdan birini tanlashni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Ikkala variant: Both the museum ___ the gallery are free.
questions.explanation: Both… and ikkisini ham qamrab oladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Juft bog‘lovchi: You can either email us nor call the office.
expected: You can either email us or call the office.
questions.explanation: Either bilan or juftlashadi.

questions.prompt: Neither…nor bilan birlashtiring: The printer is not working. The scanner is not working.
expected: Neither the printer nor the scanner is working.
questions.explanation: Ikkala birlik ega bilan neither…nor + is ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “Either Tuesday or Thursday is fine” ma’nosi: A) Ikki kundan bittasi mos. B) Ikkala kun ham yaroqsiz.
questions.explanation: Either…or muqobil tanlovni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Parallel tuzilmani tanlang: A) The course teaches not only coding but also drawing. B) The course teaches not only coding but also to draw.
questions.explanation: Not only va but also dan keyingi qismlar bir xil grammatik shaklda bo‘lishi kerak: coding va drawing.

questions.prompt: Faqat yetishmayotgan so‘zni yozing: The new pump is not only quieter ___ also cheaper.
questions.explanation: Juft bog‘lovchi not only ... but also. Quieter va cheaper parallel qiyosiy sifatlardir.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Juft bog‘lovchi: The guide not only translated ___ also explained the customs.
questions.explanation: Not only… but also juftligi kerak.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Parallel fe’llar: She not only designs houses but also building furniture.
expected: She not only designs houses but also builds furniture.
questions.explanation: Designs va builds bir xil grammatik shaklda bo‘ladi.

questions.prompt: Not only…but also bilan birlashtiring: The flat is spacious. It is affordable. The flat is bilan boshlang.
expected: The flat is not only spacious but also affordable.
The flat isn't only spacious but also affordable.
questions.explanation: Ikki sifat parallel ulanadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Parallel tuzilma: A) He enjoys not only hiking but also to swim. B) He enjoys not only hiking but also swimming.
questions.explanation: Hiking va swimming bir xil -ing shaklida keladi.

questions.prompt: Qo‘shimcha dalil kiriting; faqat mos so‘zni yozing: The hostel is close to the station. ___, breakfast is included. (Moreover / However)
questions.explanation: Ikkinchi gap yana bir afzallikni qo‘shmoqda. Moreover qo‘shimcha dalilni kiritadi.

questions.prompt: Misolni kiriting; faqat mos iborani yozing: Some metals are very light. ___, aluminium is widely used in aircraft. (For instance / As a result)
questions.explanation: Aluminium oldingi umumiy fikrga misol bo‘lmoqda. For instance misol keltirish uchun ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Misol: Many birds migrate. ___, swallows fly south in autumn. (For example / However)
questions.explanation: For example umumiy fikrga misol keltiradi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Qo‘shimcha dalil uchun however ni moreover ga almashtiring: The room is large. However, it has a balcony.
expected: The room is large. Moreover, it has a balcony.
questions.explanation: Moreover qo‘shimcha ijobiy dalilni ulaydi.

questions.prompt: Ikkinchi gap boshiga For instance qo‘shing: Some hobbies need little equipment. Walking is one example. Ikkala gapni yozing.
expected: Some hobbies need little equipment. For instance, walking is one example.
questions.explanation: For instance muayyan misolni tanishtiradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Qaysi birikma qo‘shimcha fikr kiritadi? A) In addition. B) In contrast.
questions.explanation: In addition qo‘shimcha, in contrast qarama-qarshi fikrdir.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Standart yozma ingliz tilida tinish belgilarini to‘g‘ri tanlang: A) The deadline was tight; however, we submitted the report on time. B) The deadline was tight, however, we submitted the report on time.
questions.explanation: However ikki mustaqil gapni faqat vergul bilan ulay olmaydi. Uning oldidan nuqtali vergul, keyin vergul qo‘yish to‘g‘ri.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. To‘g‘ri tinish belgili variantni tanlang: A) The ferry was full, therefore, we waited for the next one. B) The ferry was full. Therefore, we waited for the next one.
questions.explanation: Therefore oldidan nuqta qo‘yish mustaqil gaplarni to‘g‘ri ajratadi. A variantida ikki mustaqil gap faqat vergul bilan noto‘g‘ri ulangan.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Standart yozuv: A) The path was narrow, nevertheless, we continued. B) The path was narrow; nevertheless, we continued.
questions.explanation: Mustaqil gaplar orasida nuqtali vergul kerak.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. To‘g‘ri yozuv: A) We had no map. Therefore, we asked for directions. B) We had no map therefore we, asked for directions.
questions.explanation: Therefore yangi gap boshida vergul bilan ajratiladi.

questions.prompt: However bilan ikkita gap qiling: It was dark, but we found the cabin.
expected: It was dark. However, we found the cabin.
questions.explanation: Nuqta ikki mustaqil fikrni ajratadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Qaysi variant oddiy comma splice xatosidan xoli? A) The shop was shut, we went home. B) The shop was shut, so we went home.
questions.explanation: So bog‘lovchisi ikki gapni vergul orqali to‘g‘ri ulaydi.

sections.title: Week 25 · The Street Trial and Its Exceptions
sections.text:
The town closed one shopping street to cars for four Sundays so that families could walk more comfortably. Pedestrian counts rose, and a café reported stronger sales. However, the pharmacy near the far entrance received fewer older customers. Its owner supported cleaner air but said that the nearest accessible parking space was too distant. The first report celebrated the total increase without mentioning that distribution.

A transport officer proposed moving two accessible spaces closer and allowing deliveries before the pedestrian hours began. Although that would reduce the length of the completely car-free section, it might preserve access for people who could not walk far. The café owner worried that exceptions would confuse visitors, whereas the pharmacy owner thought a clear sign could explain them.

The council will continue the trial in order to test the revised arrangement. It will record both total visits and access complaints. More pedestrians are evidence of use, not proof that every resident benefits equally. A successful trial should identify which parts work and which need adjustment, rather than turn a promising change into a claim that no problems remain.

Before the second trial, a researcher spends an ordinary Sunday walking the approaches to the street. She notices that the busiest entrance has a smooth pavement, while the route from the bus stop includes a high kerb. A simple count at the central square would miss that difference. She asks volunteers to record where visitors enter and whether they turn back, without assuming why every person changes direction.

The pharmacy owner also points out that sales figures are imperfect measures of access. A customer may successfully collect medicine without buying anything extra, while another may buy several items on behalf of neighbours who stayed at home. The café's higher sales and the pharmacy's lower visitor count therefore describe different aspects of the trial. They should be reported separately rather than forced into one score.

Editor: Your article says everyone in the building supports the new roof garden. How did you establish that?
Reporter: The residents' meeting approved it, and nobody there objected.
Editor: How many flats were represented?

Reporter: I can change it to 'Residents at the meeting supported the proposal.'

Reporter: Should I remove the positive quotations?

Reporter: One resident said the garden would transform the building.

A small regional museum has received a beautiful old wooden chair from a local school. At first, the donation seemed unremarkable. The museum already owns several chairs, and visitors rarely travel across town simply to inspect another seat. The accompanying papers, however, connect this object to evening literacy classes held in the school after normal lessons.
The distinction between an object and its documented history matters. Wood can reveal how furniture was made, while a written account may explain how it was used. Neither source is complete by itself. A polished surface does not prove that a chair belonged to a particular teacher, and a family memory may confuse two similar objects.
The curator plans to display the chair beside copies of attendance records. She will describe the connection as probable rather than certain because one date remains inconsistent. Some donors worry that cautious wording makes the story less attractive. Yet uncertainty can invite visitors to investigate rather than simply admire.
The display will also explain why the classes took place at school, not in a purpose-built adult centre. The institution was available in the evenings, and its familiar setting reduced costs. The chair becomes interesting through that social context, not through an exaggerated claim that it changed history alone.

sections.text:
A science centre described its new exhibition as 'absolutely unique' and promised that visitors would be amazed. The opening survey produced a more complicated picture. Many visitors were interested in the demonstrations, but several found the instructions confusing. The exhibition was not necessarily disappointing; the route through it was simply unclear.
One report stated that visitors almost completed every activity. Another said that almost every visitor completed an activity. These sentences sound similar, yet they describe different outcomes. The first concerns how far people progressed; the second concerns how many people participated at all. A small change in adverb position can therefore alter the apparent success of the entire project.
The evaluation team rewrote its summary using specific observations. Most visitors completed at least one activity, while fewer than half reached the final station. Families described the opening demonstration as fascinating, but some were exhausted before finding the quieter area. That evidence suggests a layout problem rather than a complete failure of content.
The centre will improve signs and add seating before buying more equipment. Its next advertisement may sound less dramatic, but the practical changes are more likely to help. Visitors need an engaging experience, not a competition between the strongest adjectives in the dictionary.

Researcher: The report says customers were completely satisfied with the delivery service. Does the evidence support that wording?
Manager: Most ratings were positive. I thought the stronger phrase made the conclusion clearer.
Researcher: It actually makes it less accurate. Some customers were pleased with the speed but frustrated by damaged packaging.
Manager: So the service was satisfying but the packaging was disappointing?
Researcher: For those respondents, yes. We should distinguish the experience from the people experiencing it. Also, this sentence says we only delivered late to rural addresses.
Manager: I meant that rural addresses were the only places with late deliveries.
Researcher: Then write that directly. 'Only delivered late' can suggest lateness was the only thing we did, which is hardly a recommendation.
Manager: Language is making our vans look worse than they are.
Researcher: Precise language will help them. We can say ninety percent arrived on time, then explain the exceptions and proposed improvements.
Manager: Would that sound defensive?
Researcher: Not if the action is clear. Acknowledging an irritating problem is more convincing than calling everything absolutely perfect. Customers remember the box they received, not the adjective we preferred in a meeting.
Manager: I'll revise the summary and keep the figures beside each claim.

expected:
Advertising often promises an amazing experience, but strong adjectives tell us little without evidence. I am more interested in what a service actually does than in whether a company calls it perfect.
The science exhibition provides a useful example. Visitors enjoyed the demonstrations, yet many struggled to find their way through the building. Calling the whole exhibition disappointing would ignore its strengths. Calling it absolutely wonderful would ignore the layout problem. Specific descriptions reveal what needs to change.
Of course, advertisements are designed to attract attention. Nobody expects a poster to contain an evaluation report. A lively phrase can communicate enthusiasm and help an event reach an audience. The problem begins when excitement replaces evidence or makes a limited benefit sound universal.
I suggest looking for concrete details beside the attractive language. What proportion of deliveries arrive on time? Which activities are included? What happens when a customer has a problem? These questions are more useful than arguing about whether something is truly amazing.
Businesses can benefit from precision. A realistic promise is easier to keep, and an acknowledged weakness gives customers a reason to trust improvement. Clear information may be quieter than a slogan, but it usually lasts longer.
