sections.text:
The town clock stopped during a busy Saturday market. Within minutes, a social media post claimed that recent restoration work had damaged the mechanism. The repair company could not have caused the immediate stoppage by working that morning: its staff had left the tower two days earlier. That did not rule out every connection, but it weakened the specific story being shared.

A caretaker later found that the power supply had failed. The clock usually restarts automatically when electricity returns, but this time a protective switch stayed open. Residents should have waited for an inspection before describing the restoration as a failure.

The town now needs a communication rule. If the clock stops again, the caretaker will post a short notice at the market entrance. Unless an inspection identifies a cause, the notice will simply describe what is known. It will probably reduce speculation, although no notice can stop every rumour.

If the council had a larger maintenance budget, it could install a remote warning system. For now, a clear reporting process is more realistic. The lesson is not that residents should ignore faults. They should report them promptly while leaving room for explanations that have not yet been checked.

questions.explanation: Namunadagi mazmun va manba dalilini kuting; aynan bir xil ibora shart emas. 1–30-dars: bir so‘z, ko‘rsatish yoki o‘zbekcha izoh; hali o‘tilmagan inglizcha gapni talab qilmang. Keyin: qisqa javob + dalil. Xulosa savollarida dalildan ortiq da’vo qilmasin.

sections.transcript:
Festival director: We should have published a rain plan before selling tickets. People are asking whether Saturday's storytelling event will happen.

Volunteer: The field is wet, but it can't have flooded overnight. I walked across it this morning, and the river is still below the bank.

Festival director: Fair correction. I shouldn't have repeated that description without checking.

Volunteer: If rain continues tomorrow, we'll move the sessions into the village hall. Unless we reduce the audience, though, everyone won't fit.

Festival director: What happens to ticket holders who cannot enter?

Volunteer: We could offer a second performance. If we had more storytellers, simultaneous sessions would be possible, but we only have three.

Festival director: Two performances are likely to be tiring.

Volunteer: Then shorten each one and provide a proper break. When performers lose their voices, nobody benefits.

Festival director: I agree. We'll ask them today rather than announce a solution on their behalf.

Volunteer: And tell ticket holders the decision deadline. Uncertainty becomes harder when people don't know when they will hear more.

Festival director: I'll publish an update at six tomorrow, even if the final location is still uncertain. We could have planned better, but we can still make the remaining decisions openly.

Volunteer: That should give families enough time to change their travel plans.

sections.text:
Dilshod missed a scholarship deadline because he waited for a reference letter that was not required until the second stage. If he had read the instructions more carefully, he would have submitted his form on time. That explanation is true, but it leaves out an important detail: the application page displayed two different dates.

The earlier date applied to student forms; the later one applied to references. Both appeared under the heading deadline, without a clear description. An experienced applicant might have understood the distinction, whereas someone applying for the first time could easily confuse them.

Dilshod wishes he had asked the office instead of relying on a friend's interpretation. He also wishes the website would separate the stages more clearly. If he had submitted in time, he might be preparing for an interview now. However, he cannot know whether his application would have been selected.

The office has agreed to revise the page, though it will not reopen the completed round. Dilshod hopes to apply next year, provided the eligibility rules remain the same. He is saving his documents in a labelled folder.

The useful response combines personal responsibility with better design. Saying that applicants should simply be more careful would ignore a preventable source of confusion; blaming the website alone would ignore the value of asking questions.

sections.transcript:
Singer: I wish we'd recorded our first concert. If we had brought a second battery, the camera wouldn't have stopped halfway through.

Guitarist: True, but if I were better at checking equipment, I would have noticed the low charge before we started. It wasn't only a missing spare.

Singer: We'd have a complete film for our website now if we'd checked everything properly.

Guitarist: Perhaps. The camera position was poor as well. Even if it had kept running, several performers would have been hidden behind the speaker.

Singer: So buying a battery won't solve the whole problem.

Guitarist: Exactly. I hope the next recording is better, but we need a plan. We can borrow two cameras as long as we return them on Monday.

Singer: What would you do if you were organising it?

Guitarist: I'd make a short test recording from each position and ask someone outside the band to watch it. We know the songs so well that we might overlook missing details.

Singer: I wish the venue would let us enter earlier.

Guitarist: Let's ask. They may agree, provided we explain why. Regret is useful if it changes the next rehearsal; repeating the same complaint won't restore the lost footage.

Singer: I'll write to the manager tonight.

sections.text:
Three music groups want the same rehearsal room on Thursday evenings. The youth orchestra has the most members, the folk trio has the fewest, and the accessible singing group needs the room's level entrance. Choosing by group size alone would produce a clear answer, but not necessarily a fair one.

The centre previously gave priority to whoever booked first. That rule favoured groups with a member who could check the website during office hours. If the centre had noticed this sooner, it might have avoided several disputes. Staff should have asked who could realistically use the booking system.

A new proposal offers rotating Thursdays, with alternative rooms where suitable. The trio can rehearse upstairs, whereas the singing group cannot. The orchestra could divide into smaller sections occasionally, although doing so every week would damage its preparation.

No group must give up its preferred time permanently. However, each must explain which needs are essential and which are flexible. If a group cancels, it will have to release the slot at least two days ahead.

The fairest arrangement may not give everyone identical treatment. It should give comparable opportunities while recognising real differences. A transparent explanation of exceptions is likely to earn more trust than a simple rule whose hidden disadvantages are never discussed.

Equal treatment is attractive because it is easy to explain, but identical rules can create unequal opportunities. The rehearsal room dispute shows why a community centre needs to examine circumstances before choosing a booking policy.

The largest group is not automatically the group with the strongest claim. The singing group needs a level entrance, while the folk trio can use an upstairs room. If both were offered the same upstairs alternative, only one would gain a usable option.

Supporters of a simple booking rule may worry that exceptions invite favouritism. That concern deserves an answer. Staff should publish the reasons for each exception and distinguish essential access needs from preferences. Groups must also release cancelled slots promptly so others can benefit.

sections.title: Week 30 · Sharing a Room Fairly
sections.text:
Three groups want the community room on Thursday evenings. The choir has the most members, the homework club serves fewer people, and the craft group has attended for the longest time. Choosing only by group size would favour the choir; choosing only by history would favour the craft group. Neither rule automatically measures need.

The homework club cannot use the nearby hall because it lacks quiet tables. The choir could rehearse there, but would need help carrying a keyboard. The craft group can meet earlier if two members receive a lift. The coordinator proposes a four-week trial: homework stays in the room, choir uses the hall with transport help, and crafts meet before dinner.

Some members object that equal treatment should mean identical hours in the same place. Others argue that fair access may require different arrangements. The coordinator agrees to review attendance, travel difficulties and comments after the trial. If the alternative hall proves unsuitable, the plan will change. No group is promised permanent priority. The decision is justified by current constraints, and those constraints must remain open to challenge.

At the first review, the choir reports that carrying the keyboard takes longer than expected. The hall itself is suitable, but the promised trolley has a damaged wheel. This matters because a workable proposal on paper may depend on a small piece of equipment. The coordinator arranges a replacement rather than immediately concluding that the alternative venue is impossible.

Two craft members say that the earlier session clashes with school collection. Their original agreement had been based on the expectation of a later starting date, when a relative could help. The coordinator records the change without treating it as proof that they were uncooperative. Conditions can change after an agreement, and a fair trial needs a way to respond.

The next meeting will consider whether the room should rotate occasionally or whether a second quiet venue can be found. Attendance totals will remain useful, but they will be read beside reasons for absence. A nearly empty session may indicate lack of interest, inaccessible travel, or a temporary family commitment. The committee will not claim to know which explanation applies until it asks. Transparent decisions require not only a published rule but also an explanation of how new evidence can alter that rule.

sections.text:
A new walking map has been distributed at the visitor centre. Historic buildings are marked in blue, cafés are shown in orange, and public toilets are indicated by a familiar symbol. Yet the shortest street in the old quarter appears as an empty grey strip.

The omission was noticed by a shopkeeper whose doorway opens onto that street. Three small workshops were left out when business information was transferred from an older database. The designers were not told that the database had gaps, and the final draft was checked mainly for spelling.

Corrections are now being prepared. An online version has already been updated, while replacement paper copies will be printed next month. Existing copies are being given a small insert so visitors can find the missing workshops in the meantime.

The visitor centre's first statement said that errors had been made. That sentence acknowledged a problem but did not explain how it happened or who would prevent it recurring. A later statement described the transfer process and named the office responsible for checking business information.

Passive language is useful when the map or correction is the focus. However, it should not become a way of making responsibility disappear. Residents need both an accurate map and an understandable account of how accuracy will be protected.

sections.transcript:
Reporter: Several library books have been labelled unavailable this week. Are they being removed from the collection?

Librarian: No. They are being checked after a leak in the storage room. Some covers were damaged, but most pages are dry.

Reporter: How are the books selected for repair?

Librarian: Each one is examined by a conservation assistant. Minor damage is treated here; complicated cases are sent to a specialist. Twenty books have already been returned to the shelves.

Reporter: Were readers told what happened?

Librarian: A notice was posted at the entrance, but it wasn't added to the catalogue. People searching from home saw only the word unavailable, which understandably caused concern.

Reporter: Will that be changed?

Librarian: Yes. A short explanation will be attached to each affected record today. Readers will also be offered another edition where one exists.

Reporter: Some people say damaged books are simply thrown away.

Librarian: That hasn't happened in this case. Decisions about replacement are documented, and rare items are assessed separately. We cannot promise to save every ordinary copy, but disposal isn't our first response.

Reporter: So the important distinction is between temporary assessment and permanent withdrawal.

Librarian: Exactly. A short catalogue label can hide a long process. We need to make that process easier to understand.

sections.text:
A cracked railway sign was removed from the town museum's entrance after a visitor noticed a sharp edge. Several supporters asked why a modern copy could not be installed immediately. The curator explained that any replacement had to be distinguished clearly from the original object.

The old sign had been donated by a retired station worker. Before it reached the museum, it had been repainted twice, and parts of the lettering had been altered. Those changes made it imperfect as a guide to its original appearance, but valuable as evidence of continued use.

While a temporary board was being designed, the damaged sign was being examined by a conservator. Its surface could be stabilised, but the missing corner could not be reconstructed confidently from the available photographs. A complete replacement might therefore present an invented detail as historical fact.

The curator told supporters that a replica would be considered for outdoor use. She said the original would remain inside, accompanied by an explanation of its repairs. Neither object would be described as an untouched example.

This approach costs more effort than ordering a clean new sign. It also gives visitors a more interesting question: does an object's history end when it leaves the factory, or do later repairs become part of the history worth preserving?

sections.transcript:
Manager: The theatre seats will not be numbered for tonight's rehearsal. We told the invited audience that they could choose any place in the main section.

Usher: Can the balcony be used?

Manager: No. The lighting rail was being inspected this morning, and the area must be kept closed until the engineer signs the report.

Usher: Someone said the inspection had been completed.

Manager: The physical check had been completed by ten, but the written clearance had not been issued. Those are different stages.

Usher: I'll explain that if people ask. Should the accessible seats be reserved?

Manager: Yes. They must not be occupied by people who can use the other rows until guests needing them have arrived. Please offer a nearby alternative politely.

Usher: A parent told me her child couldn't see from the back. Could two front seats be held?

Manager: Certainly, provided they arrive before the introduction. Tell her that the sound may be loud there, so she can decide.

Usher: I'll put all that in the briefing.

Manager: Good. Don't simply repeat that the building is open. Some areas are available and others are restricted. A useful announcement should tell people what they can actually do, not leave them to discover the limits at a closed door.

sections.text:
After a residents' meeting, a message circulated saying that the council had promised to remove every roadside tree. The official notes told a different story. The engineer had said that three damaged trees required inspection and that removal was one possible outcome.

The misunderstanding began when a resident who arrived late asked whether the trees would disappear. Another participant replied that the engineer had discussed removal. In later messages, discussion became a decision, and a possible decision became a promise.

Meeting secretary Feruza has prepared a clearer summary. It identifies the speaker behind each statement and separates proposals from agreed actions. The engineer offered to inspect the trees; the council representative promised to publish the findings; residents asked the team not to begin work without notice. No general removal programme was approved.

Feruza also keeps present tense where information is still current. The trees stand beside a school, and the pavement remains narrow. Changing every verb mechanically into the past could make continuing conditions sound outdated.

Accurate reporting is more than a grammar exercise. It requires attention to what a person actually committed to and what the audience may infer. A report that preserves uncertainty can be less dramatic than a rumour, but far more useful to people planning how to respond.

sections.transcript:
Editor: Your article says the chef refused to train local students. Is that what she said?

Reporter: She said she couldn't take a group this month because the kitchen was being refurbished.

Editor: Then the sentence is too broad. Did she discuss another date?

Reporter: Yes. She offered to host four students in November and asked whether they had completed basic hygiene training.

Editor: Include that. A temporary limit isn't a refusal to help.

Reporter: She also told me not to photograph the unfinished kitchen. I wrote that she wanted to hide the conditions.

Editor: That is an interpretation. Did she give a reason?

Reporter: She said the builders had left equipment across the floor and that visitors could trip.

Editor: Report the reason she gave. If you doubt it, you need evidence, not a suggestive phrase.

Reporter: Should I mention the student who complained about the delay?

Editor: Certainly. He said he had arranged transport already, didn't he? His inconvenience is relevant. We can show both the disruption and the chef's proposed solution.

Reporter: I'll revise the headline too. It currently makes the disagreement sound permanent.

Editor: Good. Our job is to make the situation understandable. A stronger accusation might attract attention, but it should never emerge merely because a sentence lost its time limit.

criteria: Reported statement, question va request ni to‘g‘ri qayta beradi; bir defining relative bilan shaxs yoki narsani aniqlaydi.
Pozitsiyasini matndagi ikki dalil bilan asoslaydi; bitta qarshi argumentga aniq javob beradi.

questions.prompt: Mahalla forumiga yig‘ilish xabarlarini aniq tarqatish haqida post yozing. Daraxtlar misoli, qisqalik talabi va uch amaliy tekshiruvni muhokama qiling. 180–200 so‘z yozing.
expected:
A meeting summary should help neighbours understand what will happen, not simply repeat the most alarming sentence. In the tree discussion, a possible outcome became a promise as messages passed between people.

The engineer offered to inspect three damaged trees. The council representative promised to publish the findings. Those commitments are different from an agreement to remove every tree, and residents need the distinction before organising a response.

I understand why people shorten messages. A long report may be ignored, especially in a busy group chat. However, brevity should remove repetition rather than remove uncertainty. A short sentence can still name the speaker and say whether an action was proposed, promised or approved.

Before forwarding a summary, I would ask three questions. Who made the statement? What exactly did that person commit to? Is the information still current? If any answer is missing, readers should be told that clarification is needed.

We should also preserve requests from people who may be affected. Residents asked the team not to begin without notice, which is relevant even though removal was not agreed. Accurate reporting allows disagreement to remain visible without turning every concern into a confirmed event.
criteria: Voqea va va’dani farqlaydi, qisqalik e’tiroziga javob beradi va uch tekshiruv savolini taklif qiladi.
Janrga mos uslubni saqlaydi va maqsadli grammatikadan kamida ikki o‘rinli misol ishlatadi.
180–200 so‘z chegarasiga rioya qiladi; fikrlarni izchil bog‘laydi.

questions.prompt: Boshqa kun va joyda yetkazing: “I am here today,” he said. He said that bilan boshlang; here → there, today → that day.
expected: He said that he was there that day.
questions.explanation: Joy va vaqt so‘zlari yangi kontekstga moslashadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Bir kunda shu joyning o‘zida xabar berilsa, today va here: A) Kontekstga mos bo‘lsa saqlanishi mumkin. B) Har doim almashtirilishi shart.
questions.explanation: Vaqt va joy o‘zgarishi kontekstga bog‘liq.

questions.prompt: Faqat bog‘lovchini yozing: ‘Have you paid the fee?’ → The clerk asked me ___ I had paid the fee. (if / that)
questions.explanation: Ha/yo‘q savoli o‘zlashtirilganda if yoki whether bilan kiritiladi. Berilgan variantlardan if to‘g‘ri.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. ‘Is the lift working?’ savolining to‘g‘ri o‘zlashtirma shakli qaysi? A) She asked whether was the lift working. B) She asked whether the lift was working.
questions.explanation: O‘zlashtirma savolda ega yordamchi fe’ldan oldin keladi: the lift was working. Savoldagi inversiya saqlanmaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Ha/yo‘q savolini yetkazing: “Are you alone?” → He asked me ___ I was alone. If/whether dan foydalaning.
questions.explanation: Yes/no o‘zlashtirma savol if yoki whether bilan ulanadi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: So‘z tartibi: She asked whether could I hear her.
expected: She asked whether I could hear her.
questions.explanation: O‘zlashtirma savolda ega yordamchidan oldin keladi.

questions.prompt: If bilan yetkazing; The clerk asked me bilan boshlang, backshift qiling: “Do you need a receipt?”
expected: The clerk asked me if I needed a receipt.
questions.explanation: Do tushadi, need → needed; tartib oddiy gapniki.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. To‘g‘ri o‘zlashtirma savol: A) He asked that I was free. B) He asked if I was free.
questions.explanation: Ha/yo‘q savoliga that emas, if/whether kerak.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. ‘Why did the alarm ring?’ → A) He asked why the alarm had rung. B) He asked why had the alarm rung.
questions.explanation: Wh-so‘z saqlanadi, lekin keyin oddiy gap tartibi ishlatiladi: the alarm had rung. Past Simple backshift bilan Past Perfect bo‘ladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat noto‘g‘ri so‘z tartibini tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: She asked how much did the coat cost. Past Simple ni saqlang.
expected: She asked how much the coat cost.
questions.explanation: O‘zlashtirma wh-savolda did yordamchisi bilan savol tartibi ishlatilmaydi. Cost fe’lining Past Simple shakli ham cost.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Backshift: “Where do you keep the spare key?” → She asked where I ___ the spare key.
questions.explanation: Keep → kept; do tushadi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Tartibni tuzating, zamonni saqlang: He asked when would the train leave.
expected: He asked when the train would leave.
questions.explanation: Wh-so‘zdan keyin ega + fe’l tartibi ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Backshift qiling; She asked me bilan boshlang: “Why are you laughing?”
expected: She asked me why I was laughing.
questions.explanation: Why saqlanadi, are you → I was.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “He asked who had called” gapida if kerakmi? A) Yo‘q, who saqlanadi. B) Ha, who o‘rniga if shart.
questions.explanation: Wh-savol o‘z savol so‘zini saqlaydi.

questions.prompt: Buyruqni to‘ldiring; faqat bo‘shliqni yozing: ‘Fasten your seat belt,’ the pilot told me. → The pilot told me ___ my seat belt.
questions.explanation: Buyruq told + shaxs + to-infinitive orqali yetkaziladi: told me to fasten.

questions.prompt: Buyruqni to‘ldiring; faqat bo‘shliqni yozing: ‘Put on your helmets,’ the instructor told us. → The instructor told us ___ our helmets.
questions.explanation: Told us dan keyin to put on keladi. Put on birikmasining ikkala qismi ham saqlanadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Buyruq: “Check the lock,” she told me. → She told me ___ the lock.
questions.explanation: Told + shaxs + to-infinitive buyruqni yetkazadi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Buyruq qolipi: The coach told us stretch before running.
expected: The coach told us to stretch before running.
questions.explanation: Told us dan keyin to stretch kerak.

questions.prompt: Buyruqni yetkazing; The teacher told the class bilan boshlang: “Open your notebooks.”
expected: The teacher told the class to open their notebooks.
questions.explanation: Your → their, buyruq → to open.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “He told me to wait by the gate” ma’nosi: A) U darvoza yonida kutayotganini aytdi. B) Menga darvoza yonida kutishni aytdi.
questions.explanation: Object + to-infinitive boshqaga berilgan ko‘rsatmadir.

questions.prompt: Inkor buyruqni yetkazing; faqat bo‘shliqni yozing: ‘Do not feed the deer,’ the ranger told us. → The ranger told us ___ the deer.
questions.explanation: Inkor buyruqda not to + asosiy fe’l qo‘llanadi: not to feed.

questions.prompt: Inkor buyruqni yetkazing; faqat bo‘shliqni yozing: ‘Do not share the password,’ the manager told Kim. → The manager told Kim ___ the password.
questions.explanation: Told Kim dan keyin taqiq not to share shaklida beriladi; do not bu tuzilmada ishlatilmaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Inkor buyruq: “Don't lean out,” she told the child. → She told the child ___ out.
questions.explanation: Inkor buyruq not to + fe’l bilan beriladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “She told him not to switch it off” ma’nosi: A) Uni o‘chirmaslikni aytdi. B) Uni yoqmaslikni aytdi.
questions.explanation: Not switch off o‘chirishni inkor qiladi.

questions.prompt: Iltimosni ask bilan yetkazing; faqat bo‘shliqni yozing: ‘Please carry this tray,’ the waiter said to me. → The waiter asked me ___ that tray.
questions.explanation: Iltimos asked + shaxs + to-infinitive bilan yetkaziladi: asked me to carry.

questions.explanation: Asked + object + to-infinitive iltimosni yetkazadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Qaysi variantda ikkala fe’l qolipi ham to‘g‘ri? A) She offered lending a torch, but he refused taking it. B) She offered to lend a torch, but he refused to take it.
questions.explanation: Offer va refuse fe’llaridan keyin to-infinitive ishlatiladi: offered to lend va refused to take.

questions.explanation: Refuse dan keyin to-infinitive keladi.

questions.explanation: Deny dan keyin -ing keladi; oldinlik having broken bilan ham beriladi.

questions.explanation: Suggest + -ing; suggest to do emas.

questions.explanation: Admit + -ing qilingan ishni tan olishdir.

questions.explanation: Nurse odamni bildiradi, shuning uchun berilgan variantlardan who mos keladi.

questions.explanation: Chef odam bo‘lgani uchun which emas, who kerak. Who ergash gapning egasi ham hisoblanadi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Odamga who ishlating: The driver which helped us was very calm.

questions.explanation: Driver shaxs bo‘lgani uchun who mos.

questions.explanation: Who owns the bakery qaysi ayol ekanini aniqlaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “The students who arrive early can choose their seats” kimlarga tegishli? A) Erta keladigan talabalarga. B) Barcha talabalarga, kelishidan qat’i nazar.
questions.explanation: Defining relative guruhni chegaralaydi.

sections.text:
The riverside bench whose plaque carries two names has become an unexpected meeting place. It commemorates a local carpenter and a school caretaker who used to repair playground equipment together. Neither person held public office, and some residents initially questioned why their names deserved a permanent place.

The application was supported by families whose children had used the repaired equipment. They described a form of contribution that rarely appeared in newspaper reports. The carpenter, who also trained young apprentices, donated spare timber. The caretaker organised repairs during holidays, when the playground was empty.

A committee member suggested putting the names on a general list of volunteers instead. That would recognise more people, but it would remove the particular story that made this partnership meaningful. The final design therefore includes a small link to other community histories.

Visitors sitting on the bench can read a short account without opening the link. Those wanting more detail can explore photographs and interviews. The committee avoided describing the pair as people who solved every local problem. It chose to recognise a specific contribution and invite others to add further stories.

A public memorial does not have to claim that its subjects were extraordinary in every respect. Sometimes it asks people to notice ordinary work that mattered deeply to particular neighbours.

Coordinator: You asked for a mentor who works in publishing. Have you decided what kind of help you need?

Student: I want someone whose experience includes illustrated books. I'm interested in editing text that has to fit around pictures.

Coordinator: Then Samira may suit you. She works at a small press, where editors often discuss layout with designers.

Student: Is she the editor you mentioned last month?

Coordinator: Yes. Samira, who started as a translator, enjoys helping people compare different career routes. However, she prefers meeting students who have prepared specific questions.

Student: I was planning to ask her to read my entire manuscript.

Coordinator: That may be too much for an introductory meeting. You could send two pages and explain one decision you're struggling to make.

Student: Would she expect polished work?

Coordinator: No. The pages you bring should show your question clearly. A mentor isn't simply a person who tells you whether you are talented.

Student: That changes how I think about it. I had imagined waiting until everything looked impressive.

Coordinator: Students hoping to learn usually gain more from a focused problem than a flawless performance. Decide what you want to understand, and give her enough context to respond.

Student: I'll choose the scene where the picture and text repeat the same information.

questions.explanation: Ergash gap kafeda sodir bo‘ladigan harakatni bildiradi; where bu yerda at which ma’nosida.

questions.prompt: Faqat bitta so‘zni tuzating va butun gapni yozing: This is the studio which we record our podcast. Which o‘rniga joy ravishini qo‘ying.
expected: This is the studio where we record our podcast.
questions.explanation: We record our podcast gapiga joy ma’nosi kerak. Where — in which, ya’ni o‘sha studiyada degani.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Joy ravishi, where/which: This is the warehouse ___ we store the spare parts.
questions.explanation: Where joyda bajariladigan ishni bog‘laydi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Takroriy joy predlogini olib tashlang: This is the park where we play in.
expected: This is the park where we play.
questions.explanation: Where bu yerda in the park ma’nosini o‘z ichiga oladi.

questions.prompt: Where bilan birlashtiring; is tiny bilan tugating: The village is tiny. My grandparents live there.
expected: The village where my grandparents live is tiny.
questions.explanation: There o‘rnini where egallaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “the shop where I work” qaysi iboraga teng? A) the shop which I work B) the shop in which I work
questions.explanation: Where bu yerda in which bilan teng.

questions.prompt: Faqat mos so‘zni yozing: Do you recall the winter ___ the lake froze completely? (when / where)
questions.explanation: Winter vaqtni bildiradi; shu davrda sodir bo‘lgan hodisa when bilan bog‘lanadi.

questions.prompt: Vaqtni bildiruvchi nisbiy ravishni yozing: There was a period ___ our village had no electricity. (when / whose)
questions.explanation: Period vaqt oralig‘i. When ergash gapni shu davr bilan bog‘laydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Vaqt ravishi: I still remember the evening ___ the power failed. (when / where)
questions.explanation: Evening vaqtni bildiradi; when mos.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Vaqtga mos ravish: July was the month where we moved house.
expected: July was the month when we moved house.
questions.explanation: Month bilan vaqt ravishi when ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: When bilan birlashtiring: I remember the morning. We found the lost puppy then.
expected: I remember the morning when we found the lost puppy.
questions.explanation: Then o‘rnini when egallaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “the year when I graduated” gapida when nimani bog‘laydi? A) Bitirgan vaqtni. B) Bitirgan joyni.
questions.explanation: When vaqt nisbiy gapini kiritadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Qaysi gapda zarur ega olmoshi bor? A) The dog that guards the warehouse belongs to Aziz. B) The dog guards the warehouse belongs to Aziz.
questions.explanation: That guards fe’lining egasi bo‘lib kelgan. Ega vazifasidagi nisbiy olmoshni tushirib bo‘lmaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. To‘g‘ri savolni tanlang: A) Where is the parcel arrived this morning? B) Where is the parcel that arrived this morning?
questions.explanation: Arrived fe’lining egasi that. Uni olib tashlash ikki gapni grammatik bog‘lovchisiz qoldiradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Tushirib bo‘lmaydigan ega olmoshi, who/which: The architect ___ designed this library won an award.
questions.explanation: Who designed qismining egasi; uni tushirib bo‘lmaydi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Yetishmayotgan that ni qo‘shing: The bus stops outside our house is always crowded.
expected: The bus that stops outside our house is always crowded.
questions.explanation: That stops qismida that ega bo‘lib zarur.

questions.prompt: Takroriy he ni olib tashlang: The man who he delivers our bread is on holiday.
expected: The man who delivers our bread is on holiday.
questions.explanation: Who allaqachon ega, yana he kerak emas.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Qaysi gapda which ni tushirib bo‘lmaydi? A) The camera which I use is old. B) The camera which fell is broken.
questions.explanation: Which fell da which ega; I use da esa to‘ldiruvchi.

questions.prompt: Faqat to‘ldiruvchi nisbiy olmoshini olib tashlab, gapni qayta yozing: The recipe that you recommended was delicious.
expected: The recipe you recommended was delicious.
questions.explanation: That recommended fe’lining to‘ldiruvchisi; ega you bo‘lgani uchun that ni tushirish mumkin.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Qaysi gapda nisbiy olmoshni tushirish mumkin? A) The scarf which I knitted is green. B) The scarf which covers the statue is green.
questions.explanation: A da which to‘ldiruvchi, I esa ega. B da which covers fe’lining egasi, shuning uchun tushirilmaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Nisbiy olmosh tushirilgan: The person ___ I hired starts tomorrow. (who / zero) Ikkalasi mumkin bo‘lsa both yozing.
questions.explanation: Defining gapda to‘ldiruvchi who tushirilishi mumkin.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Ortiqcha it ni olib tashlang: The song I heard it yesterday is beautiful.
expected: The song I heard yesterday is beautiful.
questions.explanation: Song nisbiy qismning to‘ldiruvchisi, it takrorlanmaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat to‘ldiruvchi olmoshni olib tashlang: The hotel that you suggested has closed.
expected: The hotel you suggested has closed.
questions.explanation: You ega bo‘lgani uchun object that tushiriladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “The doctor I saw was helpful” gapida tushirilgan olmoshning vazifasi: A) To‘ldiruvchi. B) Ega.
questions.explanation: I ega, doctor esa saw fe’lining to‘ldiruvchisidir.

questions.prompt: Faqat mos olmoshni yozing: Dr Evans, ___ trained in Canada, now runs our clinic. (who / that)
questions.explanation: Vergul bilan ajratilgan qo‘shimcha ma’lumot gapida odam uchun who ishlatiladi; that ishlatilmaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat mos olmoshni yozing: Our new scanner, ___ arrived on Tuesday, is already in use. (which / that)
questions.explanation: Non-defining relative gapda narsa uchun which kerak. That vergul bilan ajratilgan bunday gapga mos emas.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Qo‘shimcha ma’lumot: My laptop, ___ is six years old, still works. (which / that)
questions.explanation: Non-defining gapda buyum uchun which ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: That o‘rniga odamga mos olmosh: Mr Lee, that lives upstairs, is a pilot.
expected: Mr Lee, who lives upstairs, is a pilot.
questions.explanation: Vergulli qo‘shimcha ma’lumotda who kerak.

questions.prompt: Which bilan qo‘shing; is electric bilan tugating, nisbiy qismni vergullar bilan ajrating: Our car is electric. It was made in Korea.
expected: Our car, which was made in Korea, is electric.
questions.explanation: Qo‘shimcha ma’lumot which bilan va ikki vergul orasida keladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Non-defining gapda which ni tushirish mumkinmi? A) Ha, har doim. B) Yo‘q.
questions.explanation: Qo‘shimcha nisbiy gapning olmoshi saqlanadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat mos so‘zni yozing: Elena, ___ daughter is a violinist, invited us to a concert. (whose / who)
questions.explanation: Daughter oldidan egalikni bildiruvchi whose ishlatiladi. Bu qo‘shimcha ma’lumotli gaplarda ham mumkin.

questions.prompt: Faqat mos so‘zni yozing: Lisbon, ___ we spent our honeymoon, has steep streets. (where / which)
questions.explanation: Ergash gapda Lisbon harakat sodir bo‘lgan joy. Where bu yerda in which ma’nosini beradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Qo‘shimcha egalik: Mr Karimov, ___ son won a scholarship, is delighted.
questions.explanation: Whose qo‘shimcha qismda ham egalikni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Joy ravishi: Samarkand, which my cousin lives, attracts many visitors. Where ishlating.
expected: Samarkand, where my cousin lives, attracts many visitors.
questions.explanation: Where my cousin lives joydagi holatni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Whose bilan qo‘shing; is a designer bilan tugating, vergullar qo‘ying: Amina is a designer. Her brother is a chef.
expected: Amina, whose brother is a chef, is a designer.
questions.explanation: Her brother → whose brother qo‘shimcha ma’lumotga aylanadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “Oxford, where I studied, is busy in summer” gapida where qismi: A) Qo‘shimcha ma’lumot. B) Qaysi Oxford ekanini zarur ajratish.
questions.explanation: Vergullar qo‘shimcha ma’lumotni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Bir nechta ammam bor; faqat shifokor bo‘lganini ajratmoqchiman. A) My aunt who is a doctor works nights. B) My aunt, who is a doctor, works nights.
questions.explanation: Qaysi amma ekanini aniqlash uchun who is a doctor zarur. Defining relative gap vergulsiz yoziladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Bitta velosipedim bor; rangini qo‘shimcha ma’lumot sifatida aytaman. A) My bicycle which is yellow needs new tyres. B) My bicycle, which is yellow, needs new tyres.
questions.explanation: Velosiped allaqachon aniq, rang esa qo‘shimcha ma’lumot. Non-defining gap ikki tomondan vergul bilan ajratiladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Faqat ko‘k nishonli ishchilar kirishi mumkin. A) Workers who have blue badges may enter. B) Workers, who have blue badges, may enter.
questions.explanation: Vergulsiz nisbiy qism kerakli guruhni ajratadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “My sons, who live abroad, visit each summer” nimani anglatadi? A) Faqat ayrim o‘g‘illarim chet elda. B) Gapdagi barcha o‘g‘illarim chet elda.
questions.explanation: Vergulli qism tilga olingan barcha o‘g‘illarga qo‘shimcha ma’lumot beradi.

questions.prompt: Qo‘shimcha ma’lumotni alohida gap qiling: My sister, who studies medicine, is twenty. Avval yoshini, keyin She bilan o‘qishini ayting.
expected: My sister is twenty. She studies medicine.
questions.explanation: Qo‘shimcha nisbiy qismni ajratsak, asosiy ma’no saqlanadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Standart yozuvda qo‘shimcha qismni to‘g‘ri ajrating: A) Our coach, who is very patient, helped us. B) Our coach, who is very patient helped us.
questions.explanation: Gap o‘rtasidagi qo‘shimcha qism ikki tomondan ajratiladi.

questions.prompt: Rasmiy uslubdagi mos olmoshni yozing: The consultant with ___ we negotiated was patient. (whom / that)
questions.explanation: Oldinga chiqarilgan predlogdan keyin odam uchun whom ishlatiladi: with whom. With that bu nisbiy tuzilmada mumkin emas.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Nisbiy gapning oddiy va rasmiy shakllari qaysi juftlikda to‘g‘ri? A) the grant I applied for / the grant for which I applied B) the grant I applied for / the grant for that I applied
questions.explanation: Oddiy uslubda predlog oxirda qolishi mumkin. Rasmiy shaklda predlog oldinga chiqsa, narsa uchun which kerak, that emas.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Rasmiy nisbiy gap: The organisation for ___ she works is expanding.
questions.explanation: Predlogdan keyin buyum/tashkilot uchun which keladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Predlogdan keyingi olmosh: The researcher to that I wrote replied.
expected: The researcher to whom I wrote replied.
questions.explanation: Odamga oid predlogdan keyin whom ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Rasmiy to whom qolipiga o‘tkazing: The woman I spoke to was the director.
expected: The woman to whom I spoke was the director.
questions.explanation: Predlogni boshga ko‘chirganda whom saqlanadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Qaysi shakl odatiy suhbat uslubida? A) the colleague with whom I travelled B) the colleague I travelled with
questions.explanation: Suhbatda predlog ko‘pincha nisbiy qism oxirida qoladi.

questions.prompt: Butun oldingi fikrga ishora qiluvchi olmoshni tanlang: The team finished two days early, ___ surprised the client. (which / what)
questions.explanation: Which bu yerda bitta otga emas, jamoaning ikki kun oldin tugatganiga ishora qiladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. ‘The bus never arrived, which made us late.’ gapida which nimaga ishora qiladi? A) Avtobusning kelmaganiga. B) Faqat bus otiga.
questions.explanation: Kechikishga avtobusning kelmagani sabab bo‘lgan. Which oldingi gapdagi butun vaziyatni anglatadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Butun fikrga ishora: Nobody objected, ___ surprised the chairperson.
questions.explanation: Which oldingi butun voqeaga ishora qiladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Butun gapga ishora: She remembered my birthday, what was thoughtful.
expected: She remembered my birthday, which was thoughtful.
questions.explanation: Oldingi fikrga which ishlatiladi, what emas.

questions.prompt: Which bilan birlashtiring: He paid for everyone's lunch. This was generous.
expected: He paid for everyone's lunch, which was generous.
questions.explanation: Which uning hamma uchun to‘laganiga ishora qiladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “The lift broke down, which delayed us” gapida which nimaga ishora qiladi? A) Liftning buzilganiga. B) Faqat liftning rangiga.
questions.explanation: Which oldingi butun holatni bog‘laydi.

questions.prompt: Who is qismini tushirib, fe’lni -ing shaklida saqlang. Butun gapni yozing: The technician who is testing the alarm needs silence.
expected: The technician testing the alarm needs silence.
questions.explanation: Faol davomiy harakatni ifodalovchi who is testing qisqartirilganda testing qoladi.

questions.prompt: Qisqartirilgan faol aniqlovchi uchun fe’l shaklini yozing: Passengers ___ to Rome should go to gate twelve. (travel)
questions.explanation: Yo‘lovchilar harakatni bajaradi, shuning uchun -ing shakli kerak. Travelling Britaniya, traveling Amerika imlosi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Qisqa faol aniqlovchi: Anyone ___ (wish) to join should email us.
questions.explanation: Faol aniqlovchida -ing ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Qisqartirilgan faol qism: The girl stand by the window is my cousin.
expected: The girl standing by the window is my cousin.
questions.explanation: Girl bajaruvchi; standing bilan aniqlanadi.

questions.prompt: Who are ni tushiring: The people who are queuing outside need tickets.
expected: The people queuing outside need tickets.
questions.explanation: Who are queuing → queuing.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “The train approaching platform two” ma’nosi: A) Ikkinchi yo‘lakka yaqinlashayotgan poyezd. B) Ikkinchi yo‘lakda ta’mirlangan poyezd.
questions.explanation: Approaching faol jarayonni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Which were qismini olib tashlab, butun gapni yozing: The samples which were collected yesterday are frozen.
expected: The samples collected yesterday are frozen.
questions.explanation: Passiv aniqlovchi qisqartirilganda V3 qoladi: collected. Namunalar harakatni bajarmaydi, ular yig‘ilgan.

questions.prompt: Qisqartirilgan passiv aniqlovchidagi fe’l shaklini yozing: The jewellery ___ from the gallery has been recovered. (steal)
questions.explanation: Zargarlik buyumlari o‘g‘irlangan, shuning uchun steal ning V3 shakli stolen kerak; stealing faol ma’no beradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Qisqa passiv aniqlovchi: The goods ___ (damage) in transit will be replaced.
questions.explanation: Goods ish ta’sirida; V3 damaged ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Qisqa passiv: The messages sending yesterday were confidential. V3 ishlating.
expected: The messages sent yesterday were confidential.
questions.explanation: Xabarlar yuborilgan; sent passiv ma’no beradi.

questions.prompt: That was ni tushiring: The bridge that was built in 1880 is still in use.
expected: The bridge built in 1880 is still in use.
questions.explanation: That was built → built qisqa passivdir.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “The forms signed by the manager” ma’nosi: A) Menejerga imzo qo‘ygan blankalar. B) Menejer imzolagan blankalar.
questions.explanation: Signed V3 blankalarga bajarilgan ishni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat qavsdagi fe’lning kerakli shaklini yozing: Do you mind ___ the window? (close)
questions.explanation: Mind fe’lidan keyin gerund, ya’ni -ing shakli keladi: mind closing.

questions.prompt: Faqat xato fe’l shaklini tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: We avoid to park near the hospital.
expected: We avoid parking near the hospital.
questions.explanation: Avoid dan keyin to-infinitive emas, -ing shakli kerak: avoid parking.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Fe’l qolipi: She admitted ___ the instructions. (ignore)
questions.explanation: Admit dan keyin -ing keladi.

expected: My cousins enjoy camping by the river.
questions.explanation: Enjoy + -ing ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Finish + -ing bilan birlashtiring: He wrote the report. He finished it at noon. He finished bilan boshlang.
expected: He finished writing the report at noon.
questions.explanation: Finish dan keyin writing kerak.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. To‘g‘ri fe’l qolipi: A) We considered moving abroad. B) We considered to move abroad.
questions.explanation: Consider odatda -ing shaklini oladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat qavsdagi fe’lning kerakli shaklini yozing: The council agreed ___ the playground. (rebuild)
questions.explanation: Agree fe’lidan keyin to-infinitive keladi: agreed to rebuild.

questions.prompt: Faqat fe’l shaklini to‘ldiring: Did the climbers manage ___ the summit? (reach)
questions.explanation: Manage to do something biror ishni uddalashni bildiradi. Shu sababli to reach kerak.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Infinitiv: They hope ___ the finals. (reach)
questions.explanation: Hope dan keyin to-infinitive keladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Decide qolipi: I decided taking the evening class.
expected: I decided to take the evening class.
questions.explanation: Decide + to-infinitive ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Plan to bilan qayta yozing: We are planning a visit to the island. We plan bilan boshlang.
expected: We plan to visit the island.
questions.explanation: Plan to visit rejalashtirilgan harakatni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. To‘g‘ri gap: A) He refused signing the receipt. B) He refused to sign the receipt.
questions.explanation: Refuse dan keyin to-infinitive kerak.

questions.prompt: Faqat fe’l shaklini yozing: The vet advised us ___ the cat indoors. (keep)
questions.explanation: Advise + shaxs + to-infinitive qolipi qo‘llanadi: advised us to keep.

questions.prompt: Faqat xato fe’l shaklini tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: The guard warned them staying away from the cliff.
expected: The guard warned them to stay away from the cliff.
questions.explanation: Warn someone to do something qolipida shaxsdan keyin to-infinitive keladi: warned them to stay.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Object + infinitive: The tutor encouraged me ___ again. (apply)
questions.explanation: Encourage + shaxs + to-infinitive.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Want qolipi: I want my brother learn to cook.
expected: I want my brother to learn to cook.
questions.explanation: Want dan keyin shaxs va to-infinitive keladi.

questions.prompt: Expect + object + to bilan yozing: I expect that the guests will arrive early.
expected: I expect the guests to arrive early.
questions.explanation: The guests infinitiv oldidagi to‘ldiruvchidir.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “She persuaded him to stay” gapida kim qoladi? A) He. B) She.
questions.explanation: Him keyingi stay harakatining bajaruvchisidir.

sections.text:
Repairing a bicycle can teach more than watching someone repair it, but only if the learner is allowed to make meaningful decisions. At the neighbourhood workshop, volunteers used to take tools from beginners whenever a job became slow. Customers left with working bicycles but depended on the same help next time.

The coordinator has changed the sessions. Volunteers now ask learners to describe the problem before touching the bicycle. They let them test simple explanations and help them compare results. Nobody is expected to handle a repair that requires specialist equipment; having a wheel professionally rebuilt remains a sensible choice.

One participant, Nargiza, remembers paying for a brake adjustment without understanding what had changed. This month she remembered to photograph the cable before loosening it. When the brake still rubbed, she tried repositioning the wheel instead of tightening every screw. The problem disappeared.

Learning this way takes patience. A volunteer may stop to explain a small movement while several people are waiting. Nevertheless, the goal is not merely to turn bicycles around quickly. It is to make future problems less mysterious.

Participants are getting used to asking why a step is necessary. Some still prefer to have everything done for them. The workshop can respect that preference while keeping its teaching sessions different from a commercial repair service.

sections.transcript:
Tutor: You remembered to bring the camera, but did you remember to charge the battery?

Learner: Yes. I also had the lens cleaned yesterday. I thought the spots in my photographs were caused by dust.

Tutor: They may have been. Let's take a test picture before changing the settings.

Learner: I keep trying to photograph birds, but they move before I can focus.

Tutor: Try focusing on the branch first. Then wait for a bird to land. You don't have to chase every movement.

Learner: That sounds easier. I'm used to taking pictures of buildings, which stay still.

Tutor: Getting used to movement takes time. Put the strap on, turn the camera on and leave the menu alone for a moment.

Learner: Should I buy a faster lens?

Tutor: Perhaps eventually, but buying equipment won't replace learning to anticipate a subject. Stop checking every photograph immediately and watch what the birds do.

Learner: I remember seeing one return to the same branch yesterday.

Tutor: Good observation. Use that pattern. We'll stop to review the pictures after ten minutes.

Learner: So the exercise is really about attention.

Tutor: Partly. Technical settings matter, but knowing when to leave them alone matters too. Let the camera help you observe instead of letting its menus consume the whole session.

criteria: Remember doing/to do va try doing/to do farqini saqlaydi; have/get something done bilan xizmatni ifodalaydi.
Pozitsiyasini matndagi ikki dalil bilan asoslaydi; bitta qarshi argumentga aniq javob beradi.
Ikki daqiqada kirish, bog‘langan asoslar va xulosani yetkazadi.

questions.prompt: 184-darsdagi mentor Samiraga rasmiy email yozing. Tajribasini nega mos deb bilishingiz, ikki sahifalik misol va qisqa uchrashuv so‘rovini bayon qiling. 120–150 so‘z yozing.
expected:
Dear Ms Samira,
The mentoring coordinator suggested contacting you because you have experience editing illustrated books. I am interested in learning how editors balance written information with visual storytelling.

I have attached two pages from a short manuscript. I tried removing several descriptive sentences, but I am not sure whether the remaining text gives readers enough context. The pictures already show most of the physical action.

Would you be willing to discuss this example in a brief meeting? I am not asking you to edit the complete manuscript. I would value understanding how you decide which details belong in the words and which can be left to the illustrations.

I will prepare specific questions and remember to bring both versions of the scene. Thank you for considering my request.

Kind regards,
Dilnoza Karimova
criteria: Mentorga mos sabab, bajarilgan tahrir tajribasi va chegaralangan aniq yordam so‘rovini beradi.
Janrga mos uslubni saqlaydi va maqsadli grammatikadan kamida ikki o‘rinli misol ishlatadi.
120–150 so‘z chegarasiga rioya qiladi; fikrlarni izchil bog‘laydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat fe’l shaklini yozing: The storm made the ferry ___ course. (change)
questions.explanation: Faol gapdagi make + to‘ldiruvchi dan keyin to siz asosiy fe’l keladi: made the ferry change.

questions.prompt: Faqat xato fe’l shaklini tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Please let the soup to cool.
questions.explanation: Let + to‘ldiruvchi + bare infinitive qolipi kerak. Cool oldidan to ishlatilmaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Bare infinitive: The funny ending made everyone ___ (laugh).
questions.explanation: Make + object dan keyin to siz infinitiv keladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Let qolipi: Let the children to choose their books.
expected: Let the children choose their books.
questions.explanation: Let + object + asosiy fe’l.

questions.prompt: Make bilan yozing: The loud noise caused the baby to wake up. The loud noise made bilan boshlang.
expected: The loud noise made the baby wake up.
questions.explanation: Made the baby dan keyin wake to siz keladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Faol gapdagi to‘g‘ri qolip: A) They made us to wait. B) They made us wait.
questions.explanation: Faol make dan keyin bare infinitive kerak.

questions.prompt: Faqat fe’l shaklini yozing: You must not ___ this switch with wet hands. (touch)
questions.explanation: Modal must dan keyin, inkor gapda ham, fe’lning to siz asosiy shakli keladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat xato fe’l shaklini tuzatib, butun savolni yozing: Could you to weigh this suitcase?
questions.explanation: Could modal fe’lidan keyin weigh keladi; to weigh ishlatilmaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Modaldan keyin: She might ___ us later. (join)
questions.explanation: Might dan keyin asosiy shakl ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Modal qolipi: He should to read the small print.
expected: He should read the small print.
questions.explanation: Should dan keyin to qo‘yilmaydi.

questions.prompt: Must bilan qayta yozing: It is essential that she checks every label. She bilan boshlang.
questions.explanation: Must dan keyin checks emas, check keladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. To‘g‘ri gap: A) The battery may need replacing. B) The battery may needs replacing.
questions.explanation: Modal ega bilan o‘zgarmaydigan asosiy fe’lni oladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat fe’l shaklini yozing: They left without ___ goodbye. (say)
questions.explanation: Without predlogidan keyin fe’l gerund shaklida keladi: without saying.

questions.prompt: Faqat fe’l shaklini yozing: Are you looking forward to ___ your cousins? (see)
questions.explanation: Look forward to birikmasidagi to predlogdir. Undan keyin infinitive emas, seeing kerak.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Predlogdan keyin: He apologised for ___ late. (arrive)
questions.explanation: For predlogidan keyin -ing ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Predlog + fe’l: We are worried about lose our luggage.
expected: We are worried about losing our luggage.
We're worried about losing our luggage.
questions.explanation: About dan keyin losing kerak.

questions.prompt: Without + -ing bilan birlashtiring: She left. She did not lock the door. She left bilan boshlang.
expected: She left without locking the door.
questions.explanation: Without locking bajarmasdan ketishni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “I look forward to meeting you” gapidagi to: A) Infinitiv belgisi. B) Predlog.
questions.explanation: Bu birikmada to predlog, undan keyin meeting keladi.

questions.prompt: Maqsadni to + fe’l bilan ifodalang; faqat bo‘shliqni yozing: We hired a van ___ the furniture. (move)
questions.explanation: Furgon yollashning maqsadi mebellarni ko‘chirish. Maqsad to move infinitivi bilan beriladi.

questions.prompt: Maqsadni to + fe’l bilan ifodalang; faqat bo‘shliqni yozing: She set an alarm ___ the early train. (catch)
questions.explanation: Budilnik qo‘yishdan maqsad poyezdga ulgurish; to catch shu maqsadni ko‘rsatadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Maqsad infinitivi: I brought a torch ___ the path. (light)
questions.explanation: To light nima maqsadda olib kelinganini bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Maqsad: She went to the post office for send a parcel. To-infinitive ishlating.
expected: She went to the post office to send a parcel.
questions.explanation: Maqsad uchun to send kerak.

questions.prompt: To bilan birlashtiring: We opened the windows. We wanted to let in fresh air.
expected: We opened the windows to let in fresh air.
questions.explanation: To let in harakat maqsadini beradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “I called to confirm the booking” gapidagi infinitiv: A) Qo‘ng‘iroq maqsadini bildiradi. B) Qo‘ng‘iroq vaqtini bildiradi.
questions.explanation: To confirm nima uchun qo‘ng‘iroq qilinganini aytadi.

questions.prompt: Gap egasini gerund shaklida yozing: ___ regularly improves your stamina. (cycle)
questions.explanation: Harakat gap egasi bo‘lganda gerund ishlatilishi mumkin: cycling. Cycle oxiridagi e tushadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Qaysi gapda -ing shakli ega vazifasida? A) We practise drawing every evening. B) Drawing requires patience.
questions.explanation: B gapida Drawing requires fe’lining egasi. A gapida drawing practise fe’lining to‘ldiruvchisi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Gerund ega: ___ vegetables at home saves money. (grow)
questions.explanation: Growing harakat nomi bo‘lib ega vazifasida keladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Gerund egaga mos fe’l: Swimming in cold water require practice.
expected: Swimming in cold water requires practice.
questions.explanation: Bitta gerund birikma birlikdagi egadir.

questions.prompt: Gerund bilan boshlang: It takes patience to learn a new script.
expected: Learning a new script takes patience.
questions.explanation: Learning a new script gap egasiga aylanadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Qaysi gapda cooking ega? A) I enjoy cooking. B) Cooking relaxes me.
questions.explanation: Cooking relaxes gapida harakat nomi egadir.

questions.prompt: Faqat fe’l shaklini yozing: We were relieved ___ the good news. (hear)
questions.explanation: Relieved sifatidan keyin hisning sababini to-infinitive bilan berish mumkin: relieved to hear.

questions.prompt: Faqat fe’l shaklini yozing: Is this device safe ___ underwater? (use)
questions.explanation: Safe sifatidan keyin to-infinitive keladi: safe to use — ishlatish xavfsiz.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Sifat + infinitiv: This label is difficult ___ in dim light. (read)
questions.explanation: Difficult dan keyin to-infinitive ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Sifat qolipi: I was pleased hearing that you had recovered. To-infinitive ishlating.
expected: I was pleased to hear that you had recovered.
questions.explanation: Pleased to hear xursandlik sababini bildiradi.

questions.prompt: It is + sifat + to qolipiga o‘tkazing: Finding this address is hard.
expected: It is hard to find this address.

questions.explanation: Sifatdan keyingi infinitiv baholanayotgan ishni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. To‘g‘ri gap: A) Are you ready to order? B) Are you ready order?
questions.explanation: Ready dan keyin to order kerak.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. ‘Quti juda og‘ir, uni ko‘tara olmayman’ ma’nosini tanlang: A) The box is too heavy for me to lift. B) The box is heavy enough for me to lift.
questions.explanation: Too + sifat + to-infinitive ortiqcha daraja harakatga to‘sqinlik qilishini bildiradi. Enough esa yetarlilikni anglatadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. ‘Narvon tomga yetadigan darajada uzun’ ma’nosini tanlang: A) The ladder is enough long to reach the roof. B) The ladder is long enough to reach the roof.
questions.explanation: Enough sifatdan keyin keladi: long enough. Undan keyin to-infinitive ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Yetarli daraja: The shelf is low ___ for a child to reach.
questions.explanation: Sifat + enough + to-infinitive.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Enough joyi: This bag is enough big to hold the tent.
expected: This bag is big enough to hold the tent.
questions.explanation: Enough sifatdan keyin keladi.

questions.prompt: Too…to bilan birlashtiring: The water is very deep. We cannot stand in it. The water bilan boshlang; for us ishlating.
expected: The water is too deep for us to stand in.
questions.explanation: Too deep chegaradan ortiq chuqurlikni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “He is too tired to concentrate” ma’nosi: A) Yetarli dam olgan. B) Charchoq sabab diqqatini jamlay olmaydi.
questions.explanation: Too…to natijani amalga oshirishga to‘siqni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: U endi tirnog‘ini tishlamaydi. Faqat mos shaklni yozing: He stopped ___ his nails. (biting / to bite)
questions.explanation: Stop + -ing o‘sha harakatni to‘xtatishni bildiradi: tirnoq tishlashni bas qildi.

questions.prompt: Sayyohlar yurishni vaqtincha to‘xtatib, xaritani tekshirishdi. Faqat mos shaklni yozing: The hikers stopped ___ the map. (checking / to check)
questions.explanation: Stop to do boshqa harakatni bajarish uchun to‘xtashni bildiradi. Bu yerda yurish xaritani tekshirish uchun to‘xtatilgan.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Odatdan voz kechdi: She stopped ___ fizzy drinks last month. (drinking / to drink)
questions.explanation: Stop doing shu ishni bas qilishdir.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Maqsad uchun to‘xtadi: We stopped buying petrol on our way home. Ma’no: benzin olish uchun yo‘lda to‘xtadik; to-infinitive ishlating.
expected: We stopped to buy petrol on our way home.
questions.explanation: Stop to do boshqa ishni qilish uchun to‘xtashdir.

questions.prompt: Stop + -ing bilan yozing: The baby no longer cried. The baby stopped bilan boshlang.
questions.explanation: Stopped crying yig‘lash tugaganini bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “She stopped to answer her phone” ma’nosi: A) Telefoniga javob berish uchun to‘xtadi. B) Telefoniga javob berishni butunlay bas qildi.
questions.explanation: To answer to‘xtash maqsadidir.

questions.prompt: Bajarilishi kerak bo‘lgan ishni eslatyapsiz. Faqat mos shaklni yozing: Remember ___ the plants before you leave. (watering / to water)
questions.explanation: Remember to do hali bajarilishi kerak bo‘lgan ishni esdan chiqarmaslikni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Bolaligimdagi voqea xotiramda. Faqat mos shaklni yozing: I will never forget ___ the ocean for the first time. (seeing / to see)
questions.explanation: Forget doing o‘tmishda sodir bo‘lgan voqeani unutish bilan bog‘liq. Never forget seeing — ko‘rganimni hech qachon unutmayman.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Bajarilishi kerak ish: Don't forget ___ the door before bed. (locking / to lock)
questions.explanation: Forget to do bajarilishi kerak ishni unutishdir.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Voqea xotirasi: I remember to meet her at school ten years ago. -ing ishlating.
expected: I remember meeting her at school ten years ago.
questions.explanation: Remember doing oldingi voqeani eslashdir.

questions.prompt: Remember to bilan eslatma yozing: You must bring your ID tomorrow.
expected: Remember to bring your ID tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Remember to bring kelajakdagi ishni eslatadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “I remembered posting the letter” ma’nosi: A) Xat jo‘natishni endi rejalashtirdim. B) Xatni jo‘natganim xotiramga keldi.
questions.explanation: Remembered doing oldingi bajarilgan ish xotirasidir.

questions.prompt: Yechim sifatida usulni sinab ko‘rishni tavsiya qiling: If the sauce is too sour, try ___ a little honey. (adding / to add) Faqat shaklni yozing.
questions.explanation: Try doing bir usulni sinab, natijasini ko‘rishni bildiradi; bu yerda asal qo‘shish tajriba sifatida taklif qilinmoqda.

questions.prompt: Urinish bo‘lgan, lekin ish amalga oshmagan. Faqat mos shaklni yozing: I tried ___ the fallen tree, but it was too heavy. (lifting / to lift)
questions.explanation: Try to do qiyin ishni bajarishga urinishni bildiradi. Daraxtni ko‘tarish bu yerda muvaffaqiyatsiz bo‘lgan.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Tajriba sifatida usul: Try ___ the router closer to the laptop. (moving / to move)
questions.explanation: Try doing muammoni yechish uchun usulni sinashdir.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Qiyin urinish, muvaffaqiyatsiz: He tried reaching the top shelf, but he was too short. To-infinitive ishlating.
expected: He tried to reach the top shelf, but he was too short.
questions.explanation: Try to do ishni bajarishga urinishni ta’kidlaydi.

questions.prompt: Try + -ing bilan maslahat bering: Perhaps sleeping with an extra pillow will help. Try bilan boshlang.
expected: Try sleeping with an extra pillow.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “I tried to keep my eyes open, but fell asleep” ma’nosi: A) Uyg‘oq qolishga urindim, ammo uddalay olmadim. B) Uyg‘oq qolish usulini muvaffaqiyatli sinadim.

questions.prompt: Avvalgi, hozir yo‘q odatni ifodalang; faqat fe’l shaklini yozing: I used to ___ stamps, but I no longer do. (collect)

questions.prompt: Hozirgi ko‘nikkanlikni ifodalang; faqat fe’l shaklini yozing: The baker is used to ___ before dawn. (work)
questions.explanation: Be used to birikmasi ko‘nikkanlikni bildiradi. Bu yerdagi to predlog bo‘lgani uchun working kerak.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Ko‘nikkanlik: We are used to ___ in a noisy office. (work)
questions.explanation: Be used to dan keyin -ing keladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Oldingi odat: She used to living above a shop.
expected: She used to live above a shop.
questions.explanation: Used to + asosiy fe’l oldingi odatdir.

questions.prompt: Be used to bilan yozing: Speaking in public is familiar and comfortable for him. He bilan boshlang.
expected: He is used to speaking in public.
He's used to speaking in public.
questions.explanation: Be used to doing o‘rganib qolganlikni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “I used to get up at five” ma’nosi: A) Hozir beshda turishga ko‘nikish jarayonidaman. B) Ilgari beshda turardim.

questions.prompt: Faqat fe’l shaklini yozing: It took me a month to get used to ___ on the left. (drive)
questions.explanation: Get used to ko‘nikish jarayonini bildiradi; to dan keyin -ing shakli keladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Yangi sharoitga ko‘nikish ma’nosidagi to‘g‘ri gapni tanlang: A) The puppy is getting used to its new home. B) The puppy is getting use to its new home.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Ko‘nikish jarayoni: I am getting used to ___ contact lenses. (wear)

expected: They soon got used to living in a small town.
questions.explanation: To bu yerda predlog; living kerak.

questions.prompt: Get used to bilan yozing: Gradually, the new timetable became familiar to me. I gradually bilan boshlang, Past Simple.
expected: I gradually got used to the new timetable.
questions.explanation: Got used to moslashish tugaganini bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “You will get used to the noise” ma’nosi: A) Shovqinga asta-sekin ko‘nikasiz. B) Ilgari shovqin qilardingiz.
questions.explanation: Get used to yangi sharoitga moslashishdir.

sections.text:
The community centre is collecting recipes from older residents, but its first exhibition raised an unexpected problem. Several dishes were labelled traditional without identifying whose tradition was meant. Visitors from different families recognised the names but disagreed about ingredients and preparation.

Archive volunteer Yusuf interviewed the contributors again. One cook explained that she had replaced almonds with apricot kernels when almonds were expensive. Another said her mother used to steam a dish that neighbouring families baked. These differences had been removed during editing because the team wanted short, consistent recipe cards.

The revised archive preserves the variations. Each card identifies the contributor and includes a brief note about changes over time. Recipes donated by people who prefer privacy are listed under chosen names, with permission recorded separately. Contributors are invited to check the final wording before publication.

Some visitors would prefer a single correct version. However, the archive is intended to document lived practice, not settle every culinary argument. A neat standard recipe could be less faithful to that purpose than several slightly different accounts.

Yusuf has learned to ask what editing removes as well as what it improves. Keeping a detail that seems inconvenient may preserve the very evidence that makes an ordinary recipe historically interesting.

sections.transcript:
Filmmaker: The subtitles have been checked twice. Are we ready to show the interview?

Translator: Almost. There is one sentence that could misrepresent the speaker. He said his family had moved because work was difficult to find. The subtitle says they were forced to leave.

Filmmaker: Isn't that a reasonable summary?

Translator: It adds a degree of pressure he didn't state. We should ask him whether that wording reflects what he meant.

Filmmaker: We invited him to review the film, but he hasn't replied.

Translator: Then keep the narrower wording for now. Silence cannot be treated as agreement.

Filmmaker: What about the joke near the end? A literal translation sounds strange.

Translator: We can adapt that, provided the humour remains directed at the same situation. I suggest adding a short phrase rather than replacing it with an unrelated local joke.

Filmmaker: The audience who saw the rough version liked the stronger sentence.

Translator: That doesn't make it more accurate. People whose experiences are being presented deserve to recognise their own meaning.

Filmmaker: You're right. I'll get the subtitle changed and send him the revised section.

Translator: Good. Editing should help viewers understand the speaker. It shouldn't quietly turn him into the character we think would make a more dramatic film.

expected:
A community recipe archive should preserve more than instructions for producing a meal. It can show how families responded to changing prices, available ingredients and personal preferences. Removing every variation would lose some of that history.

One contributor explained that she had replaced almonds with apricot kernels when almonds became expensive. That detail tells us something about daily life which a standard ingredient list cannot reveal. Recipes collected from different households should therefore retain their sources and meaningful differences.

There is a practical objection: visitors may find several versions confusing when they simply want to cook. The archive can address this by separating the main method from short historical notes. Readers who need instructions can follow them, while others can explore the context.

Contributors should also be invited to check how their words are presented. A polished card is not necessarily an accurate one, particularly if an editor has removed an explanation that seemed inconvenient.

I would publish a clear recipe beside a brief account of its development and links to related versions. This approach allows the archive to remain useful in a kitchen without pretending that a living tradition has only one authorised form.
