questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “She said she hadn't received the letter” ma’nosi: A) Xatni olmaganini aytdi. B) Xatni olganini aytdi.
questions.explanation: Not inkor ma’nosini o‘zlashtirma gapda saqlaydi.

questions.prompt: Present Continuous ni Past Continuous ga o‘tkazing; faqat bo‘shliqni yozing: Omar said, ‘I am measuring the wall.’ → Omar said that he ___ the wall.
questions.explanation: Davomiy zamonning backshift shakli was/were + -ing: am measuring → was measuring.

questions.prompt: Present Simple ni Past Simple ga o‘tkazing; faqat fe’lni yozing: Lila said, ‘My uncle owns a bakery.’ → Lila said that her uncle ___ a bakery.
questions.explanation: Owns hozirgi zamondan owned o‘tgan zamoniga o‘zgaradi. Egalik ma’nosi saqlanadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Present Continuous ni ortga suring: “I am feeding the birds,” she said. → She said that she ___ the birds.
questions.explanation: Am feeding → was feeding.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Backshift talab qilinadi: “We live nearby,” they said. → They said that they live nearby.
expected: They said that they lived nearby.
questions.explanation: Present Simple backshift bilan Past Simple ga o‘tadi.

questions.prompt: Backshift qiling; He said that bilan boshlang: “I am learning Korean,” he said.
expected: He said that he was learning Korean.
questions.explanation: Hozirgi davomiy zamon o‘tgan davomiyga o‘tadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “I work nights” gapining backshift shakli: A) She said she had worked nights. B) She said she worked nights.
questions.explanation: Present Simple bir pog‘ona Past Simple ga o‘tadi.

questions.prompt: Past Simple ni Past Perfect ga suring; faqat bo‘shliqni yozing: Ben said, ‘I broke the handle.’ → Ben said that he ___ the handle.
questions.explanation: Broke ning Past Perfect shakli had broken: had + break fe’lining uchinchi shakli.

questions.prompt: Present Perfect ni Past Perfect ga suring; faqat bo‘shliqni yozing: Ada said, ‘I have checked the figures.’ → Ada said that she ___ the figures.
questions.explanation: Have checked backshift qilinganda had checked bo‘ladi; sifatdosh checked o‘zgarmaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Past Simple ni ortga suring: “I left the keys at home,” he said. → He said that he ___ the keys at home.
questions.explanation: Left → had left backshiftidir.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Perfect backshift: “We have eaten,” they said. → They said that they had ate.
expected: They said that they had eaten.
questions.explanation: Had dan keyin V3 eaten kerak.

questions.prompt: Backshift qiling; Malika said that bilan boshlang: “I have lost my receipt,” Malika said.
expected: Malika said that she had lost her receipt.
questions.explanation: Have lost → had lost; my → her.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “He said he had broken the cup” gapida qaysi ish oldin? A) Piyolani sindirish. B) Bu haqda aytish.
questions.explanation: Past Perfect xabar berishdan oldingi ishni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Modal fe’lni ortga suring; faqat bo‘shliqni yozing: Dan said, ‘I will reserve a table.’ → Dan said that he ___ reserve a table.
questions.explanation: O‘zlashtirma gapda will ning backshift shakli would. Undan keyin reserve asosiy shaklda keladi.

questions.prompt: Modal fe’lni ortga suring; faqat bo‘shliqni yozing: Rosa said, ‘I can translate this menu.’ → Rosa said that she ___ translate that menu.
questions.explanation: Can o‘zlashtirma gapda could ga o‘tadi. Bu yerda tarjima qila olish qobiliyati xabar qilinmoqda.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Backshift: “We will wait outside,” they said. → They said that they ___ wait outside.
questions.explanation: Will o‘tgan xabarda would bo‘ladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Modal backshift: “I can juggle,” he said. → He said that he could juggled.
expected: He said that he could juggle.
questions.explanation: Can → could; keyingi fe’l asosiy shaklda qoladi.

questions.prompt: Backshift qiling; She said that bilan boshlang: “I will send the invoice,” she said.
expected: She said that she would send the invoice.
She said that she'd send the invoice.
questions.explanation: Will → would o‘tmish nuqtasidan kelajakni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “I can lift it” gapining modal backshifti: A) He said he must lift it. B) He said he could lift it.
questions.explanation: Qobiliyat can dan could ga o‘tadi.

questions.prompt: Xabar hozir aytilmoqda. Zamonni ortga surmang; faqat fe’lni yozing: Farida says, ‘I teach biology.’ → Farida says that she ___ biology.
questions.explanation: Says hozirgi zamonda bo‘lgani uchun backshift kerak emas. She egasi bilan teach ga -es qo‘shiladi.

questions.prompt: Hali ham to‘g‘ri bo‘lgan ilmiy faktni backshift qilmasdan to‘ldiring: The lecturer said that the Earth ___ around the Sun. (moves / moved)
questions.explanation: Umumiy ilmiy haqiqatni hozirgi zamonda saqlash mumkin. Topshiriq zamonni ortga surmaslikni so‘rayapti, shuning uchun moves tanlanadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Hozirgi xabar, backshift yo‘q: Amir says, “I own two bikes.” → Amir says that he ___ two bikes.
questions.explanation: Says hozirgi zamonda; owns saqlanadi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Zamonni ortga surmang: “I am ready,” she says. → She says that she were ready.
expected: She says that she is ready.
questions.explanation: Hozirgi xabarda is ready keladi.

questions.prompt: Hali to‘g‘ri ilmiy faktni backshiftsiz yozing; The teacher said that bilan boshlang: “Ice floats on water.”
expected: The teacher said that ice floats on water.
questions.explanation: Hali dolzarb umumiy haqiqat Present Simple da qolishi mumkin.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Hali ham to‘g‘ri ma’lumot haqida: A) Backshift qilmaslik mumkin. B) Har doim Past Perfect shart.
questions.explanation: Dolzarblik saqlansa, zamonni saqlash mumkin.

questions.prompt: Faqat egalik olmoshini yozing: Mark said, ‘My passport has expired.’ → Mark said that ___ passport had expired.
questions.explanation: My so‘zi dastlab Markka tegishli. Mark haqida boshqa kishi xabar berganda his bo‘ladi.

questions.prompt: Men ayol kishiman. Tom menga ‘You are the winner,’ dedi. Faqat ega olmoshini yozing: Tom told me that ___ was the winner.
questions.explanation: Tomning you olmoshi gapni hozir yetkazayotgan menga tegishli, shuning uchun I ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Qizlar gapirdi: “Our bags are heavy,” the girls said. → The girls said that ___ bags were heavy.
questions.explanation: Our xabar qiluvchilar nuqtasidan their ga o‘tadi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Erkakning o‘z telefoni: Jasur said, “My phone is broken.” → Jasur said that my phone was broken.
expected: Jasur said that his phone was broken.
questions.explanation: My Jasurning telefoni bo‘lgani uchun his bo‘ladi.

questions.prompt: Ali menga “I will help you,” dedi. Ali told me that bilan boshlang, backshift qiling.
expected: Ali told me that he would help me.
Ali told me that he'd help me.
questions.explanation: I → he, you → me; olmoshlar ishtirokchilarga qarab o‘zgaradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “We are ready,” the players said. O‘zlashtirma gapda we o‘rniga: A) I. B) They.
questions.explanation: Players uchinchi shaxs ko‘plik bo‘lib they ga o‘tadi.

questions.prompt: Dushanba kuni Leo ‘I will return tomorrow,’ dedi. Buni payshanba kuni yetkazyapsiz. Tomorrow o‘rniga the bilan boshlanuvchi iborani yozing: Leo said he would return ___.
questions.explanation: Boshqa kuni xabar berilganda tomorrow asl gap aytilgan kundan keyingi kunni bildiradi: the next day yoki the following day.

questions.prompt: Mira muzeyda ‘I work here,’ dedi. Endi boshqa binodasiz. Here o‘rniga mos bitta so‘zni yozing: Mira said she worked ___.
questions.explanation: Xabar boshqa joydan berilayotgani uchun here o‘rniga there keladi; muzey nazarda tutilmoqda.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Bir hafta keyin yetkazyapsiz: “I saw her yesterday,” he said. → He said he had seen her ___. The bilan boshlang.
questions.explanation: Yesterday boshqa kun nuqtasidan the day before bo‘ladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Boshqa haftada xabar bering: “I'll call next week,” she said. → She said she would call next week. Next week ni the bilan boshlanuvchi iboraga almashtiring.
expected: She said she would call the following week.
She said she would call the next week.
She said she'd call the following week.
She said she'd call the next week.
questions.explanation: Vaqt nuqtasi o‘zgargani uchun the following week kerak.

questions.prompt: Boshqa kun va joyda yetkazing: “I am here today,” he said. He said that bilan boshlang; here → there, today → that day.
expected: He said that he was there that day.
questions.explanation: Joy va vaqt so‘zlari yangi kontekstga moslashadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Bir kunda shu joyning o‘zida xabar berilsa, today va here: A) Kontekstga mos bo‘lsa saqlanishi mumkin. B) Har doim almashtirilishi shart.
questions.explanation: Vaqt va joy o‘zgarishi kontekstga bog‘liq.

questions.prompt: Faqat bog‘lovchini yozing: ‘Have you paid the fee?’ → The clerk asked me ___ I had paid the fee. (if / that)
questions.explanation: Ha/yo‘q savoli o‘zlashtirilganda if yoki whether bilan kiritiladi. Berilgan variantlardan if to‘g‘ri.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. ‘Is the lift working?’ savolining to‘g‘ri o‘zlashtirma shakli qaysi? A) She asked whether was the lift working. B) She asked whether the lift was working.
questions.explanation: O‘zlashtirma savolda ega yordamchi fe’ldan oldin keladi: the lift was working. Savoldagi inversiya saqlanmaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Ha/yo‘q savolini yetkazing: “Are you alone?” → He asked me ___ I was alone. If/whether dan foydalaning.
questions.explanation: Yes/no o‘zlashtirma savol if yoki whether bilan ulanadi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: So‘z tartibi: She asked whether could I hear her.
expected: She asked whether I could hear her.
questions.explanation: O‘zlashtirma savolda ega yordamchidan oldin keladi.

questions.prompt: If bilan yetkazing; The clerk asked me bilan boshlang, backshift qiling: “Do you need a receipt?”
expected: The clerk asked me if I needed a receipt.
questions.explanation: Do tushadi, need → needed; tartib oddiy gapniki.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. To‘g‘ri o‘zlashtirma savol: A) He asked that I was free. B) He asked if I was free.
questions.explanation: Ha/yo‘q savoliga that emas, if/whether kerak.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. ‘Why did the alarm ring?’ → A) He asked why the alarm had rung. B) He asked why had the alarm rung.
questions.explanation: Wh-so‘z saqlanadi, lekin keyin oddiy gap tartibi ishlatiladi: the alarm had rung. Past Simple backshift bilan Past Perfect bo‘ladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat noto‘g‘ri so‘z tartibini tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: She asked how much did the coat cost. Past Simple ni saqlang.
expected: She asked how much the coat cost.
questions.explanation: O‘zlashtirma wh-savolda did yordamchisi bilan savol tartibi ishlatilmaydi. Cost fe’lining Past Simple shakli ham cost.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Backshift: “Where do you keep the spare key?” → She asked where I ___ the spare key.
questions.explanation: Keep → kept; do tushadi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Tartibni tuzating, zamonni saqlang: He asked when would the train leave.
expected: He asked when the train would leave.
questions.explanation: Wh-so‘zdan keyin ega + fe’l tartibi ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Backshift qiling; She asked me bilan boshlang: “Why are you laughing?”
expected: She asked me why I was laughing.
questions.explanation: Why saqlanadi, are you → I was.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “He asked who had called” gapida if kerakmi? A) Yo‘q, who saqlanadi. B) Ha, who o‘rniga if shart.
questions.explanation: Wh-savol o‘z savol so‘zini saqlaydi.

questions.prompt: Buyruqni to‘ldiring; faqat bo‘shliqni yozing: ‘Fasten your seat belt,’ the pilot told me. → The pilot told me ___ my seat belt.
questions.explanation: Buyruq told + shaxs + to-infinitive orqali yetkaziladi: told me to fasten.

questions.prompt: Buyruqni to‘ldiring; faqat bo‘shliqni yozing: ‘Put on your helmets,’ the instructor told us. → The instructor told us ___ our helmets.
questions.explanation: Told us dan keyin to put on keladi. Put on birikmasining ikkala qismi ham saqlanadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Buyruq: “Check the lock,” she told me. → She told me ___ the lock.
questions.explanation: Told + shaxs + to-infinitive buyruqni yetkazadi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Buyruq qolipi: The coach told us stretch before running.
expected: The coach told us to stretch before running.
questions.explanation: Told us dan keyin to stretch kerak.

questions.prompt: Buyruqni yetkazing; The teacher told the class bilan boshlang: “Open your notebooks.”
expected: The teacher told the class to open their notebooks.
questions.explanation: Your → their, buyruq → to open.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “He told me to wait by the gate” ma’nosi: A) U darvoza yonida kutayotganini aytdi. B) Menga darvoza yonida kutishni aytdi.
questions.explanation: Object + to-infinitive boshqaga berilgan ko‘rsatmadir.

questions.prompt: Inkor buyruqni yetkazing; faqat bo‘shliqni yozing: ‘Do not feed the deer,’ the ranger told us. → The ranger told us ___ the deer.
questions.explanation: Inkor buyruqda not to + asosiy fe’l qo‘llanadi: not to feed.

questions.prompt: Inkor buyruqni yetkazing; faqat bo‘shliqni yozing: ‘Do not share the password,’ the manager told Kim. → The manager told Kim ___ the password.
questions.explanation: Told Kim dan keyin taqiq not to share shaklida beriladi; do not bu tuzilmada ishlatilmaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Inkor buyruq: “Don't lean out,” she told the child. → She told the child ___ out.
questions.explanation: Inkor buyruq not to + fe’l bilan beriladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Inkor tartibi: The guide told us to not to cross the rope.
expected: The guide told us not to cross the rope.
questions.explanation: Standart qolip told us not to cross.

questions.prompt: Buyruqni yetkazing; The librarian told me bilan boshlang: “Don't write in the book.”
expected: The librarian told me not to write in the book.
questions.explanation: Don’t write → not to write.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “She told him not to switch it off” ma’nosi: A) Uni o‘chirmaslikni aytdi. B) Uni yoqmaslikni aytdi.
questions.explanation: Not switch off o‘chirishni inkor qiladi.

questions.prompt: Iltimosni ask bilan yetkazing; faqat bo‘shliqni yozing: ‘Please carry this tray,’ the waiter said to me. → The waiter asked me ___ that tray.
questions.explanation: Iltimos asked + shaxs + to-infinitive bilan yetkaziladi: asked me to carry.

questions.prompt: Faqat xato fe’l shaklini tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: The visitor asked us showing her the exit.
expected: The visitor asked us to show her the exit.
questions.explanation: Ask someone to do something qolipi kerak. Showing o‘rniga to show ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Iltimos: “Please send me the link,” Sara said to Ali. → Sara asked Ali ___ her the link.
questions.explanation: Asked + object + to-infinitive iltimosni yetkazadi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Iltimos qolipi: He asked me holding the door.
expected: He asked me to hold the door.
questions.explanation: Asked me dan keyin to hold kerak.

questions.prompt: Ask bilan yetkazing; She asked me bilan boshlang: “Please help my sister.”
expected: She asked me to help her sister.
questions.explanation: Please alohida takrorlanmaydi; my → her.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “The neighbour asked us to turn the music down” ma’nosi: A) Musiqa haqida ma’lumot so‘radi. B) Ovozini pasaytirishni iltimos qildi.
questions.explanation: Ask + shaxs + to-fe’l harakatni iltimos qiladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat qavsdagi fe’lning kerakli shaklini yozing: The courier promised ___ before sunset. (return)
questions.explanation: Promise dan keyin to-infinitive keladi: promised to return — qaytishga va’da berdi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Qaysi variantda ikkala fe’l qolipi ham to‘g‘ri? A) She offered lending a torch, but he refused taking it. B) She offered to lend a torch, but he refused to take it.
questions.explanation: Offer va refuse fe’llaridan keyin to-infinitive ishlatiladi: offered to lend va refused to take.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Reporting verb: She refused ___ the agreement. (sign)
questions.explanation: Refuse dan keyin to-infinitive keladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Offer qolipi: He offered carrying my suitcase.
expected: He offered to carry my suitcase.
questions.explanation: Offer + to-infinitive yordam taklifidir.

questions.prompt: Promise bilan yetkazing; He promised bilan boshlang: “I will repay the money.”
expected: He promised to repay the money.
questions.explanation: Promise to repay va’da berishni ifodalaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “She offered to drive us home” ma’nosi: A) Olib borishni taklif qildi. B) Olib borishdan bosh tortdi.
questions.explanation: Offered taklif, refused esa bosh tortishdir.

questions.prompt: Faqat qavsdagi fe’lning kerakli shaklini yozing: The designer suggested ___ a larger font. (use)
questions.explanation: Suggest dan keyin bevosita fe’l kelsa, -ing shakli ishlatiladi: suggested using.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. A) He admitted to scratch the desk but denied to break the lamp. B) He admitted scratching the desk but denied breaking the lamp.
questions.explanation: Admit va deny dan keyin gerund kelishi mumkin: admitted scratching, denied breaking. A variantidagi to + asosiy fe’l noto‘g‘ri.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Reporting verb: The boy denied ___ the window. (break)
questions.explanation: Deny dan keyin -ing keladi; oldinlik having broken bilan ham beriladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Suggest qolipi: She suggested to postpone the picnic.
questions.explanation: Suggest + -ing; suggest to do emas.

questions.prompt: Admit + -ing bilan yozing: “I copied the answer,” he said. He admitted bilan boshlang.
expected: He admitted having copied the answer.
questions.explanation: Admit + -ing qilingan ishni tan olishdir.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “He denied taking the money” ma’nosi: A) Pulni olganini tan oldi. B) Pulni olganini inkor qildi.
questions.explanation: Denied inkor qilishni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Odamni aniqlovchi olmoshni tanlang; faqat javobni yozing: The nurse ___ treated my ankle was very gentle. (who / which)
questions.explanation: Nurse odamni bildiradi, shuning uchun berilgan variantlardan who mos keladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat xato olmoshni almashtirib, butun gapni yozing. Who ishlating: Do you know the chef which won the prize?
expected: Do you know the chef who won the prize?
questions.explanation: Chef odam bo‘lgani uchun which emas, who kerak. Who ergash gapning egasi ham hisoblanadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Odamni aniqlang; who/which: The volunteer ___ teaches chess also runs the club.
questions.explanation: Who odamni aniqlovchi nisbiy olmoshdir.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Odamga who ishlating: The driver which helped us was very calm.
expected: The driver who helped us was very calm.
questions.explanation: Driver shaxs bo‘lgani uchun who mos.

questions.prompt: Who bilan birlashtiring; is my aunt bilan tugating: The woman is my aunt. She owns the bakery.
expected: The woman who owns the bakery is my aunt.
questions.explanation: Who owns the bakery qaysi ayol ekanini aniqlaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “The students who arrive early can choose their seats” kimlarga tegishli? A) Erta keladigan talabalarga. B) Barcha talabalarga, kelishidan qat’i nazar.
questions.explanation: Defining relative guruhni chegaralaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat mos olmoshni yozing: The battery ___ powers this sensor is tiny. (which / who)
questions.explanation: Battery narsa bo‘lgani uchun which qo‘llanadi. Bu aniqlovchi gapda that ham mumkin, ammo variantlarda which berilgan.

questions.prompt: Bo‘shliqqa which yoki that dan mos keladiganini yozing: Is this the cable ___ connects the printer to the laptop?
questions.explanation: Narsani aniqlovchi defining relative gapda which ham, that ham ishlatilishi mumkin.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Buyumni aniqlang; which/that dan foydalaning: The lamp ___ stands by the sofa is solar-powered.
questions.explanation: Buyum uchun defining relative da which yoki that ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Olmoshni tuzating, which ishlating: The software who controls the heating has failed.
expected: The software which controls the heating has failed.
questions.explanation: Software shaxs emas, shuning uchun which kerak.

questions.prompt: That bilan birlashtiring: The jacket is waterproof. I bought it yesterday.
expected: The jacket that I bought yesterday is waterproof.
questions.explanation: That I bought yesterday buyumni aniqlaydi; it tushadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “The key that opens the cellar is rusty” gapida that nimaga ishora qiladi? A) Cellar ga. B) Key ga.
questions.explanation: Nisbiy qism key otini aniqlaydi.

questions.prompt: Egalikni bildiruvchi bitta nisbiy olmoshni yozing: The athlete ___ coach retired is looking for a new trainer.
questions.explanation: Murabbiy sportchiga tegishli ekanini whose coach birikmasi ko‘rsatadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat mos so‘zni yozing: Have you met the artist ___ paintings hang in the lobby? (who / whose)
questions.explanation: Paintings oldidan egalik bildiruvchi whose kerak: rasmlari vestibyulda osilgan rassom.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Egalik: The woman ___ bicycle was stolen called the police.
questions.explanation: Whose keyingi otning egasini bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Egalik olmoshi: The singer who's voice we heard is Uzbek.
expected: The singer whose voice we heard is Uzbek.
questions.explanation: Whose egalik; who’s esa who is yoki who has.

questions.prompt: Whose bilan birlashtiring: I met a boy. His father repairs clocks.
expected: I met a boy whose father repairs clocks.
questions.explanation: His father o‘rniga whose father keladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “The tree whose branches broke is very old” gapida whose buyumga ishlatilishi mumkinmi? A) Ha. B) Yo‘q, faqat odamlarga.
questions.explanation: Whose odamlar bilan birga buyumlarning egaligini ham ko‘rsatadi.

questions.prompt: Joyni ifodalovchi where yoki which ni tanlang: We found a café ___ cyclists can refill their bottles. Faqat so‘zni yozing.
questions.explanation: Ergash gap kafeda sodir bo‘ladigan harakatni bildiradi; where bu yerda at which ma’nosida.

questions.prompt: Faqat bitta so‘zni tuzating va butun gapni yozing: This is the studio which we record our podcast. Which o‘rniga joy ravishini qo‘ying.
expected: This is the studio where we record our podcast.
questions.explanation: We record our podcast gapiga joy ma’nosi kerak. Where — in which, ya’ni o‘sha studiyada degani.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Joy ravishi, where/which: This is the warehouse ___ we store the spare parts.
questions.explanation: Where joyda bajariladigan ishni bog‘laydi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Takroriy joy predlogini olib tashlang: This is the park where we play in.
expected: This is the park where we play.
questions.explanation: Where bu yerda in the park ma’nosini o‘z ichiga oladi.

questions.prompt: Where bilan birlashtiring; is tiny bilan tugating: The village is tiny. My grandparents live there.
expected: The village where my grandparents live is tiny.
questions.explanation: There o‘rnini where egallaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “the shop where I work” qaysi iboraga teng? A) the shop which I work B) the shop in which I work
questions.explanation: Where bu yerda in which bilan teng.

questions.prompt: Faqat mos so‘zni yozing: Do you recall the winter ___ the lake froze completely? (when / where)
questions.explanation: Winter vaqtni bildiradi; shu davrda sodir bo‘lgan hodisa when bilan bog‘lanadi.

questions.prompt: Vaqtni bildiruvchi nisbiy ravishni yozing: There was a period ___ our village had no electricity. (when / whose)
questions.explanation: Period vaqt oralig‘i. When ergash gapni shu davr bilan bog‘laydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Vaqt ravishi: I still remember the evening ___ the power failed. (when / where)
questions.explanation: Evening vaqtni bildiradi; when mos.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Vaqtga mos ravish: July was the month where we moved house.
expected: July was the month when we moved house.
questions.explanation: Month bilan vaqt ravishi when ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: When bilan birlashtiring: I remember the morning. We found the lost puppy then.
expected: I remember the morning when we found the lost puppy.
questions.explanation: Then o‘rnini when egallaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “the year when I graduated” gapida when nimani bog‘laydi? A) Bitirgan vaqtni. B) Bitirgan joyni.
questions.explanation: When vaqt nisbiy gapini kiritadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Qaysi gapda zarur ega olmoshi bor? A) The dog that guards the warehouse belongs to Aziz. B) The dog guards the warehouse belongs to Aziz.
questions.explanation: That guards fe’lining egasi bo‘lib kelgan. Ega vazifasidagi nisbiy olmoshni tushirib bo‘lmaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. To‘g‘ri savolni tanlang: A) Where is the parcel arrived this morning? B) Where is the parcel that arrived this morning?
questions.explanation: Arrived fe’lining egasi that. Uni olib tashlash ikki gapni grammatik bog‘lovchisiz qoldiradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Tushirib bo‘lmaydigan ega olmoshi, who/which: The architect ___ designed this library won an award.
questions.explanation: Who designed qismining egasi; uni tushirib bo‘lmaydi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Yetishmayotgan that ni qo‘shing: The bus stops outside our house is always crowded.
expected: The bus that stops outside our house is always crowded.
questions.explanation: That stops qismida that ega bo‘lib zarur.

questions.prompt: Takroriy he ni olib tashlang: The man who he delivers our bread is on holiday.
expected: The man who delivers our bread is on holiday.
questions.explanation: Who allaqachon ega, yana he kerak emas.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Qaysi gapda which ni tushirib bo‘lmaydi? A) The camera which I use is old. B) The camera which fell is broken.
questions.explanation: Which fell da which ega; I use da esa to‘ldiruvchi.

questions.prompt: Faqat to‘ldiruvchi nisbiy olmoshini olib tashlab, gapni qayta yozing: The recipe that you recommended was delicious.
expected: The recipe you recommended was delicious.
questions.explanation: That recommended fe’lining to‘ldiruvchisi; ega you bo‘lgani uchun that ni tushirish mumkin.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Qaysi gapda nisbiy olmoshni tushirish mumkin? A) The scarf which I knitted is green. B) The scarf which covers the statue is green.
questions.explanation: A da which to‘ldiruvchi, I esa ega. B da which covers fe’lining egasi, shuning uchun tushirilmaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Nisbiy olmosh tushirilgan: The person ___ I hired starts tomorrow. (who / zero) Ikkalasi mumkin bo‘lsa both yozing.
questions.explanation: Defining gapda to‘ldiruvchi who tushirilishi mumkin.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Ortiqcha it ni olib tashlang: The song I heard it yesterday is beautiful.
expected: The song I heard yesterday is beautiful.
questions.explanation: Song nisbiy qismning to‘ldiruvchisi, it takrorlanmaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat to‘ldiruvchi olmoshni olib tashlang: The hotel that you suggested has closed.
expected: The hotel you suggested has closed.
questions.explanation: You ega bo‘lgani uchun object that tushiriladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “The doctor I saw was helpful” gapida tushirilgan olmoshning vazifasi: A) To‘ldiruvchi. B) Ega.
questions.explanation: I ega, doctor esa saw fe’lining to‘ldiruvchisidir.

questions.prompt: Faqat mos olmoshni yozing: Dr Evans, ___ trained in Canada, now runs our clinic. (who / that)
questions.explanation: Vergul bilan ajratilgan qo‘shimcha ma’lumot gapida odam uchun who ishlatiladi; that ishlatilmaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat mos olmoshni yozing: Our new scanner, ___ arrived on Tuesday, is already in use. (which / that)
questions.explanation: Non-defining relative gapda narsa uchun which kerak. That vergul bilan ajratilgan bunday gapga mos emas.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Qo‘shimcha ma’lumot: My laptop, ___ is six years old, still works. (which / that)
questions.explanation: Non-defining gapda buyum uchun which ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: That o‘rniga odamga mos olmosh: Mr Lee, that lives upstairs, is a pilot.
expected: Mr Lee, who lives upstairs, is a pilot.
questions.explanation: Vergulli qo‘shimcha ma’lumotda who kerak.

questions.prompt: Which bilan qo‘shing; is electric bilan tugating, nisbiy qismni vergullar bilan ajrating: Our car is electric. It was made in Korea.
expected: Our car, which was made in Korea, is electric.
questions.explanation: Qo‘shimcha ma’lumot which bilan va ikki vergul orasida keladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Non-defining gapda which ni tushirish mumkinmi? A) Ha, har doim. B) Yo‘q.
questions.explanation: Qo‘shimcha nisbiy gapning olmoshi saqlanadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat mos so‘zni yozing: Elena, ___ daughter is a violinist, invited us to a concert. (whose / who)
questions.explanation: Daughter oldidan egalikni bildiruvchi whose ishlatiladi. Bu qo‘shimcha ma’lumotli gaplarda ham mumkin.

questions.prompt: Faqat mos so‘zni yozing: Lisbon, ___ we spent our honeymoon, has steep streets. (where / which)
questions.explanation: Ergash gapda Lisbon harakat sodir bo‘lgan joy. Where bu yerda in which ma’nosini beradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Qo‘shimcha egalik: Mr Karimov, ___ son won a scholarship, is delighted.
questions.explanation: Whose qo‘shimcha qismda ham egalikni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Joy ravishi: Samarkand, which my cousin lives, attracts many visitors. Where ishlating.
expected: Samarkand, where my cousin lives, attracts many visitors.
questions.explanation: Where my cousin lives joydagi holatni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Whose bilan qo‘shing; is a designer bilan tugating, vergullar qo‘ying: Amina is a designer. Her brother is a chef.
expected: Amina, whose brother is a chef, is a designer.
questions.explanation: Her brother → whose brother qo‘shimcha ma’lumotga aylanadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “Oxford, where I studied, is busy in summer” gapida where qismi: A) Qo‘shimcha ma’lumot. B) Qaysi Oxford ekanini zarur ajratish.
questions.explanation: Vergullar qo‘shimcha ma’lumotni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Bir nechta ammam bor; faqat shifokor bo‘lganini ajratmoqchiman. A) My aunt who is a doctor works nights. B) My aunt, who is a doctor, works nights.
questions.explanation: Qaysi amma ekanini aniqlash uchun who is a doctor zarur. Defining relative gap vergulsiz yoziladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Bitta velosipedim bor; rangini qo‘shimcha ma’lumot sifatida aytaman. A) My bicycle which is yellow needs new tyres. B) My bicycle, which is yellow, needs new tyres.
questions.explanation: Velosiped allaqachon aniq, rang esa qo‘shimcha ma’lumot. Non-defining gap ikki tomondan vergul bilan ajratiladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Faqat ko‘k nishonli ishchilar kirishi mumkin. A) Workers who have blue badges may enter. B) Workers, who have blue badges, may enter.
questions.explanation: Vergulsiz nisbiy qism kerakli guruhni ajratadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “My sons, who live abroad, visit each summer” nimani anglatadi? A) Faqat ayrim o‘g‘illarim chet elda. B) Gapdagi barcha o‘g‘illarim chet elda.
questions.explanation: Vergulli qism tilga olingan barcha o‘g‘illarga qo‘shimcha ma’lumot beradi.

questions.prompt: Qo‘shimcha ma’lumotni alohida gap qiling: My sister, who studies medicine, is twenty. Avval yoshini, keyin She bilan o‘qishini ayting.
expected: My sister is twenty. She studies medicine.
questions.explanation: Qo‘shimcha nisbiy qismni ajratsak, asosiy ma’no saqlanadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Standart yozuvda qo‘shimcha qismni to‘g‘ri ajrating: A) Our coach, who is very patient, helped us. B) Our coach, who is very patient helped us.
questions.explanation: Gap o‘rtasidagi qo‘shimcha qism ikki tomondan ajratiladi.

questions.prompt: Rasmiy uslubdagi mos olmoshni yozing: The consultant with ___ we negotiated was patient. (whom / that)
questions.explanation: Oldinga chiqarilgan predlogdan keyin odam uchun whom ishlatiladi: with whom. With that bu nisbiy tuzilmada mumkin emas.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Nisbiy gapning oddiy va rasmiy shakllari qaysi juftlikda to‘g‘ri? A) the grant I applied for / the grant for which I applied B) the grant I applied for / the grant for that I applied
questions.explanation: Oddiy uslubda predlog oxirda qolishi mumkin. Rasmiy shaklda predlog oldinga chiqsa, narsa uchun which kerak, that emas.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Rasmiy nisbiy gap: The organisation for ___ she works is expanding.
questions.explanation: Predlogdan keyin buyum/tashkilot uchun which keladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Predlogdan keyingi olmosh: The researcher to that I wrote replied.
expected: The researcher to whom I wrote replied.
questions.explanation: Odamga oid predlogdan keyin whom ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Rasmiy to whom qolipiga o‘tkazing: The woman I spoke to was the director.
expected: The woman to whom I spoke was the director.
questions.explanation: Predlogni boshga ko‘chirganda whom saqlanadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Qaysi shakl odatiy suhbat uslubida? A) the colleague with whom I travelled B) the colleague I travelled with
questions.explanation: Suhbatda predlog ko‘pincha nisbiy qism oxirida qoladi.

questions.prompt: Butun oldingi fikrga ishora qiluvchi olmoshni tanlang: The team finished two days early, ___ surprised the client. (which / what)
questions.explanation: Which bu yerda bitta otga emas, jamoaning ikki kun oldin tugatganiga ishora qiladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. ‘The bus never arrived, which made us late.’ gapida which nimaga ishora qiladi? A) Avtobusning kelmaganiga. B) Faqat bus otiga.
questions.explanation: Kechikishga avtobusning kelmagani sabab bo‘lgan. Which oldingi gapdagi butun vaziyatni anglatadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Butun fikrga ishora: Nobody objected, ___ surprised the chairperson.
questions.explanation: Which oldingi butun voqeaga ishora qiladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Butun gapga ishora: She remembered my birthday, what was thoughtful.
expected: She remembered my birthday, which was thoughtful.
questions.explanation: Oldingi fikrga which ishlatiladi, what emas.

questions.prompt: Which bilan birlashtiring: He paid for everyone's lunch. This was generous.
expected: He paid for everyone's lunch, which was generous.
questions.explanation: Which uning hamma uchun to‘laganiga ishora qiladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “The lift broke down, which delayed us” gapida which nimaga ishora qiladi? A) Liftning buzilganiga. B) Faqat liftning rangiga.
questions.explanation: Which oldingi butun holatni bog‘laydi.

questions.prompt: Who is qismini tushirib, fe’lni -ing shaklida saqlang. Butun gapni yozing: The technician who is testing the alarm needs silence.
expected: The technician testing the alarm needs silence.
questions.explanation: Faol davomiy harakatni ifodalovchi who is testing qisqartirilganda testing qoladi.

questions.prompt: Qisqartirilgan faol aniqlovchi uchun fe’l shaklini yozing: Passengers ___ to Rome should go to gate twelve. (travel)
questions.explanation: Yo‘lovchilar harakatni bajaradi, shuning uchun -ing shakli kerak. Travelling Britaniya, traveling Amerika imlosi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Qisqa faol aniqlovchi: Anyone ___ (wish) to join should email us.
questions.explanation: Faol aniqlovchida -ing ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Qisqartirilgan faol qism: The girl stand by the window is my cousin.
expected: The girl standing by the window is my cousin.
questions.explanation: Girl bajaruvchi; standing bilan aniqlanadi.

questions.prompt: Who are ni tushiring: The people who are queuing outside need tickets.
expected: The people queuing outside need tickets.
questions.explanation: Who are queuing → queuing.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “The train approaching platform two” ma’nosi: A) Ikkinchi yo‘lakka yaqinlashayotgan poyezd. B) Ikkinchi yo‘lakda ta’mirlangan poyezd.
questions.explanation: Approaching faol jarayonni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Which were qismini olib tashlab, butun gapni yozing: The samples which were collected yesterday are frozen.
expected: The samples collected yesterday are frozen.
questions.explanation: Passiv aniqlovchi qisqartirilganda V3 qoladi: collected. Namunalar harakatni bajarmaydi, ular yig‘ilgan.

questions.prompt: Qisqartirilgan passiv aniqlovchidagi fe’l shaklini yozing: The jewellery ___ from the gallery has been recovered. (steal)
questions.explanation: Zargarlik buyumlari o‘g‘irlangan, shuning uchun steal ning V3 shakli stolen kerak; stealing faol ma’no beradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Qisqa passiv aniqlovchi: The goods ___ (damage) in transit will be replaced.
questions.explanation: Goods ish ta’sirida; V3 damaged ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Qisqa passiv: The messages sending yesterday were confidential. V3 ishlating.
expected: The messages sent yesterday were confidential.
questions.explanation: Xabarlar yuborilgan; sent passiv ma’no beradi.

questions.prompt: That was ni tushiring: The bridge that was built in 1880 is still in use.
expected: The bridge built in 1880 is still in use.
questions.explanation: That was built → built qisqa passivdir.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “The forms signed by the manager” ma’nosi: A) Menejerga imzo qo‘ygan blankalar. B) Menejer imzolagan blankalar.
questions.explanation: Signed V3 blankalarga bajarilgan ishni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat qavsdagi fe’lning kerakli shaklini yozing: Do you mind ___ the window? (close)
questions.explanation: Mind fe’lidan keyin gerund, ya’ni -ing shakli keladi: mind closing.

questions.prompt: Faqat xato fe’l shaklini tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: We avoid to park near the hospital.
expected: We avoid parking near the hospital.
questions.explanation: Avoid dan keyin to-infinitive emas, -ing shakli kerak: avoid parking.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Fe’l qolipi: She admitted ___ the instructions. (ignore)
questions.explanation: Admit dan keyin -ing keladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Enjoy qolipi: My cousins enjoy to camp by the river.
expected: My cousins enjoy camping by the river.
questions.explanation: Enjoy + -ing ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Finish + -ing bilan birlashtiring: He wrote the report. He finished it at noon. He finished bilan boshlang.
expected: He finished writing the report at noon.
questions.explanation: Finish dan keyin writing kerak.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. To‘g‘ri fe’l qolipi: A) We considered moving abroad. B) We considered to move abroad.
questions.explanation: Consider odatda -ing shaklini oladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat qavsdagi fe’lning kerakli shaklini yozing: The council agreed ___ the playground. (rebuild)
questions.explanation: Agree fe’lidan keyin to-infinitive keladi: agreed to rebuild.

questions.prompt: Faqat fe’l shaklini to‘ldiring: Did the climbers manage ___ the summit? (reach)
questions.explanation: Manage to do something biror ishni uddalashni bildiradi. Shu sababli to reach kerak.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Infinitiv: They hope ___ the finals. (reach)
questions.explanation: Hope dan keyin to-infinitive keladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Decide qolipi: I decided taking the evening class.
expected: I decided to take the evening class.
questions.explanation: Decide + to-infinitive ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Plan to bilan qayta yozing: We are planning a visit to the island. We plan bilan boshlang.
expected: We plan to visit the island.
questions.explanation: Plan to visit rejalashtirilgan harakatni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. To‘g‘ri gap: A) He refused signing the receipt. B) He refused to sign the receipt.
questions.explanation: Refuse dan keyin to-infinitive kerak.

questions.prompt: Faqat fe’l shaklini yozing: The vet advised us ___ the cat indoors. (keep)
questions.explanation: Advise + shaxs + to-infinitive qolipi qo‘llanadi: advised us to keep.

questions.prompt: Faqat xato fe’l shaklini tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: The guard warned them staying away from the cliff.
expected: The guard warned them to stay away from the cliff.
questions.explanation: Warn someone to do something qolipida shaxsdan keyin to-infinitive keladi: warned them to stay.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Object + infinitive: The tutor encouraged me ___ again. (apply)
questions.explanation: Encourage + shaxs + to-infinitive.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Want qolipi: I want my brother learn to cook.
expected: I want my brother to learn to cook.
questions.explanation: Want dan keyin shaxs va to-infinitive keladi.

questions.prompt: Expect + object + to bilan yozing: I expect that the guests will arrive early.
expected: I expect the guests to arrive early.
questions.explanation: The guests infinitiv oldidagi to‘ldiruvchidir.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “She persuaded him to stay” gapida kim qoladi? A) He. B) She.
questions.explanation: Him keyingi stay harakatining bajaruvchisidir.

questions.prompt: Faqat fe’l shaklini yozing: The storm made the ferry ___ course. (change)
questions.explanation: Faol gapdagi make + to‘ldiruvchi dan keyin to siz asosiy fe’l keladi: made the ferry change.

questions.prompt: Faqat xato fe’l shaklini tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Please let the soup to cool.
questions.explanation: Let + to‘ldiruvchi + bare infinitive qolipi kerak. Cool oldidan to ishlatilmaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Bare infinitive: The funny ending made everyone ___ (laugh).
questions.explanation: Make + object dan keyin to siz infinitiv keladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Let qolipi: Let the children to choose their books.
expected: Let the children choose their books.
questions.explanation: Let + object + asosiy fe’l.

questions.prompt: Make bilan yozing: The loud noise caused the baby to wake up. The loud noise made bilan boshlang.
expected: The loud noise made the baby wake up.
questions.explanation: Made the baby dan keyin wake to siz keladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. Faol gapdagi to‘g‘ri qolip: A) They made us to wait. B) They made us wait.
questions.explanation: Faol make dan keyin bare infinitive kerak.

questions.prompt: Faqat fe’l shaklini yozing: You must not ___ this switch with wet hands. (touch)
questions.explanation: Modal must dan keyin, inkor gapda ham, fe’lning to siz asosiy shakli keladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat xato fe’l shaklini tuzatib, butun savolni yozing: Could you to weigh this suitcase?
questions.explanation: Could modal fe’lidan keyin weigh keladi; to weigh ishlatilmaydi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Modaldan keyin: She might ___ us later. (join)
questions.explanation: Might dan keyin asosiy shakl ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Modal qolipi: He should to read the small print.
expected: He should read the small print.
questions.explanation: Should dan keyin to qo‘yilmaydi.

questions.prompt: Must bilan qayta yozing: It is essential that she checks every label. She bilan boshlang.
questions.explanation: Must dan keyin checks emas, check keladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. To‘g‘ri gap: A) The battery may need replacing. B) The battery may needs replacing.
questions.explanation: Modal ega bilan o‘zgarmaydigan asosiy fe’lni oladi.

questions.prompt: Faqat fe’l shaklini yozing: They left without ___ goodbye. (say)
questions.explanation: Without predlogidan keyin fe’l gerund shaklida keladi: without saying.

questions.prompt: Faqat fe’l shaklini yozing: Are you looking forward to ___ your cousins? (see)
questions.explanation: Look forward to birikmasidagi to predlogdir. Undan keyin infinitive emas, seeing kerak.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Predlogdan keyin: He apologised for ___ late. (arrive)
questions.explanation: For predlogidan keyin -ing ishlatiladi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Predlog + fe’l: We are worried about lose our luggage.
expected: We are worried about losing our luggage.
We're worried about losing our luggage.
questions.explanation: About dan keyin losing kerak.

questions.prompt: Without + -ing bilan birlashtiring: She left. She did not lock the door. She left bilan boshlang.
expected: She left without locking the door.
questions.explanation: Without locking bajarmasdan ketishni bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Faqat A yoki B ni yozing. “I look forward to meeting you” gapidagi to: A) Infinitiv belgisi. B) Predlog.
questions.explanation: Bu birikmada to predlog, undan keyin meeting keladi.

questions.prompt: Maqsadni to + fe’l bilan ifodalang; faqat bo‘shliqni yozing: We hired a van ___ the furniture. (move)
questions.explanation: Furgon yollashning maqsadi mebellarni ko‘chirish. Maqsad to move infinitivi bilan beriladi.

questions.prompt: Maqsadni to + fe’l bilan ifodalang; faqat bo‘shliqni yozing: She set an alarm ___ the early train. (catch)
questions.explanation: Budilnik qo‘yishdan maqsad poyezdga ulgurish; to catch shu maqsadni ko‘rsatadi.

questions.prompt: Faqat bo‘shliqni to‘ldiring: Maqsad infinitivi: I brought a torch ___ the path. (light)
questions.explanation: To light nima maqsadda olib kelinganini bildiradi.

questions.prompt: Ko‘rsatilgan xatoni tuzatib, butun gapni yozing: Maqsad: She went to the post office for send a parcel. To-infinitive ishlating.
expected: She went to the post office to send a parcel.
questions.explanation: Maqsad uchun to send kerak.

questions.prompt: To bilan birlashtiring: We opened the windows. We wanted to let in fresh air.
expected: We opened the windows to let in fresh air.
questions.explanation: To let in harakat maqsadini beradi.

sections.title: Week 31 · Whose Story Is Being Preserved?
sections.text:
A local archive asked residents to describe their first jobs. The interviews were recorded with permission, and volunteers were asked to prepare short extracts. One editor removed a speaker's account of leaving a factory because it interrupted an otherwise cheerful story. Another changed 'I wanted different work' to 'I had no choice', believing the stronger phrase would hold listeners' attention.

When the speakers reviewed the extracts, both requested changes. One said that the difficult departure explained why the later job mattered. The other said that the edited phrase exaggerated the pressure he had experienced. The archive restored the missing section and replaced the stronger wording with the speaker's own account.

The team still intends to shorten interviews. However, it now records significant edits and asks contributors to check them. People who prefer not to be identified can choose a public name while their consent record is kept separately. A concise extract can remain faithful to a complex life, but only if clarity does not become an excuse to remove the meaning that belongs to the speaker. Audience interest matters; it does not replace the contributor's authority over what they meant.

The editor asks how much checking is practical when many interviews are waiting. The archive decides to prioritise changes that affect cause, responsibility, consent or the speaker's attitude. Minor pauses can usually be removed without changing meaning, but joining two answers from different questions may create a statement the contributor never made. Such a change requires particular care.

A contributor who cannot use email is offered a printed transcript and a short meeting. The team does not treat a missing online reply as approval. It records which version each person reviewed, so that a later edit is not accidentally covered by consent given to an earlier one. This takes time, but it makes the process understandable to both volunteers and speakers.

For the exhibition, listeners can hear the short extract and read a note explaining where the full interview is available. Some recordings remain private at the contributor's request. The archive therefore cannot promise unrestricted access to every source. Instead, it can explain its selection and restrictions honestly. Preserving a person's story includes respecting what that person agreed to share, even when an unavailable passage would have made the exhibition more dramatic or convenient to organise.

sections.text:
The central square has become cooler since temporary shade sails were installed above the benches. Afternoon visitors stay longer because they can sit comfortably, and families have begun using the space after school. However, the change has not benefited every nearby business equally.

A café beside the shaded area reports more customers, whereas a kiosk behind one of the support posts has become harder to see. Its owner supports the cooling project but wants the layout adjusted. She argues that a public improvement should not hide an existing business unnecessarily.

Although the first evaluation celebrated increased footfall, it did not record where people stopped or which routes they took. Consequently, the total concealed important differences within the square. Due to the position of one sail, the kiosk's sign was almost invisible from the main entrance.

The designers have proposed moving the sign and narrowing the sail slightly. Despite losing a small amount of shade, visitors would retain most of the cooling benefit. The café owner has also offered to display directions to the kiosk.

The disagreement is not evidence that the project failed. Rather, it shows why a useful evaluation must look beyond an overall improvement. A design can be successful enough to keep and imperfect enough to change.

sections.transcript:
Host: Listeners noticed that our local history podcast is shorter this month. Did we run out of material?

Producer: Quite the opposite. We recorded so much that each episode lost its focus. Because every interview contained something interesting, we kept adding sections.

Host: Yet several listeners enjoyed the detail.

Producer: They did. However, others stopped listening before the central story was explained. A long episode isn't automatically a deeper one.

Host: What have we changed?

Producer: We now build each episode around one question. Extra interviews remain available in a separate collection, so interested listeners can explore them afterwards.

Host: Does that create more work?

Producer: A little. Despite the shorter running time, editing takes longer because every transition must earn its place. We also write clearer descriptions for the additional recordings.

Host: Some contributors may feel disappointed if their voices appear only in the extra material.

Producer: That's why we explain the structure before recording. The main episode offers a route through the subject, whereas the collection preserves a wider range of experiences.

Host: So accessibility and detail aren't necessarily opponents.

Producer: Exactly. Since people have different amounts of time, we can offer different ways in. The shorter format should make the story easier to follow without suggesting that the omitted experiences are unimportant.

sections.text:
Several shops have agreed to refill visitors' water bottles without requiring a purchase. The town placed blue stickers in their windows so that walkers could identify participating businesses. Before the scheme began, organisers checked both tap access and staff availability.

The first map listed every volunteer shop, but it did not show opening hours. As a result, walkers sometimes reached a closed door. The revised version includes hours and a note advising people to carry some water in case a shop is unexpectedly unavailable. That is a precaution, not a claim that the network usually fails.

Shopkeepers can either fill bottles themselves or direct visitors to a clearly marked tap. Neither method should interrupt food preparation or block a narrow service area. In order to avoid confusion, the sticker explains which method each shop uses.

One owner worried that free water would replace drink sales. Another believed it might attract customers. The organisers will compare comments and sales patterns after the summer rather than promise either outcome now.

The network offers not only drinking water but also a reason for visitors to enter unfamiliar shops. Nevertheless, that wider benefit should be treated as a possibility. A practical service can justify itself without every advantage being exaggerated in the announcement.

questions.prompt: What can careful survey wording fix, and what can it not fix alone?
expected: It can limit claims appropriately but cannot solve every sampling problem.
criteria: A survey of the arts centre began with an enthusiastic headline: almost everyone enjoyed the exhibition.

questions.explanation: Namunadagi mazmun va manba dalilini kuting; aynan bir xil ibora shart emas. 1–30-dars: bir so‘z, ko‘rsatish yoki o‘zbekcha izoh; hali o‘tilmagan inglizcha gapni talab qilmang. Keyin: qisqa javob + dalil. Xulosa savollarida dalildan ortiq da’vo qilmasin.

sections.text:
A survey of the arts centre began with an enthusiastic headline: almost everyone enjoyed the exhibition. The list of responses was long, and nobody on the organising team doubted that visitors had a positive experience. Yet the headline depended on a small word doing a large amount of work.

Only people who completed the digital form were counted. Several visitors asked for paper, but the desk had none. Others left before reaching the final screen, where the satisfaction question appeared. The number of completed forms was therefore different from the number of visitors.

The exhibition itself was engaging. A beautiful old wooden cabinet held tools used by local craftspeople, and the accompanying interviews were fascinating. Acknowledging the survey's limits does not require pretending the display was disappointing.

Nevertheless, precision matters when results influence future spending. Most respondents enjoyed the exhibition is supported by the evidence. Most residents enjoyed it is not, because many residents never attended. Everyone was delighted is stronger still and ignores even the negative responses that were collected.

The centre plans to offer a paper form next time and record how many visitors respond. Better wording will not solve every sampling problem, but it can stop a limited finding from becoming an unlimited claim. Enthusiasm is useful; accurate enthusiasm is more useful.

Guest: Your advert described the room as completely quiet. I could hear deliveries every morning.

Owner: I'm sorry. Most guests find it quiet, but the bakery next door receives flour at seven.

Guest: Then completely is misleading. I wasn't expecting silence all day, but that word influenced my choice.

Owner: You're right. I should say the room faces a courtyard and is usually quiet outside delivery hours.

Guest: The photograph also showed a large desk.

Owner: There is a desk, but it may look larger because of the camera angle. It's a small square wooden table, really.

Guest: I was planning to work there for a week. A precise description would have helped.

Owner: I'll add the measurements. The room is comfortable for holidays, but not everyone needs the same facilities.

Guest: Exactly. I wasn't disappointed by an ugly room. I was disappointed by the difference between the description and the practical conditions.

Owner: Would a desk in the shared lounge help for the remaining days?

Guest: Yes, provided it is available in the mornings.

Owner: It is. I'll reserve it and update the advert tonight.

Guest: Thank you. Specific information will probably attract guests whose needs fit the room better, even if the description sounds less impressive.

Small words can change the size of a claim. Almost everyone enjoyed an exhibition sounds close to universal approval, but the meaning depends on who was asked and whose answers were included.

At the arts centre, only completed digital forms were counted. Visitors who wanted paper could not respond in that way, and some people never reached the final question. The list of answers is useful, but it does not represent every visitor automatically.

A better headline would say that most respondents enjoyed the exhibition. This is still positive, and it identifies the group behind the conclusion. Nobody needs to describe an engaging display as disappointing just because the survey has limitations.

sections.text:
A regional rail operator is considering a quiet carriage on its busiest afternoon service. Passengers have asked whether calls will be prohibited and where families with young children will sit. The operator's first announcement answered neither question, saying only that a calmer journey was being developed.

Passenger representative Kamila supports the idea but wants practical details. She asks, 'Could you explain how staff will be handling complaints?' A rule that depends on passengers confronting one another could create more tension than it removes.

The proposed carriage will not be silent. Door announcements will continue, and passengers will be talking when they need assistance. The aim is to discourage sustained loud conversations and phone calls, not prevent every necessary sound. Staff will be checking the arrangement during a four week introduction period.

Some commuters think the plan is unnecessary. Others, including people who find noise exhausting, see a real benefit. Kamila is thinking about both groups when she suggests clear signs and an alternative carriage with no special restrictions.

A good consultation should make disagreement specific. Asking whether people like quiet is less useful than asking how the rule will operate and what will happen when needs conflict. Courtesy is not simply a polite tone; it includes giving people enough information to make a reasonable choice.

sections.transcript:
Colleague: Could you tell me whether the meeting room is free tomorrow morning?

Coordinator: It is until eleven. After that, the design team will be using it for interviews.

Colleague: We won't be disturbing them if we finish at half past ten, will we?

Coordinator: No, but please leave ten minutes to put the chairs back. They need a different layout.

Colleague: So do we. I think our group will need a circle rather than rows.

Coordinator: That's fine. I'm thinking about moving the spare tables today to make more space.

Colleague: Do you know where the portable screen is?

Coordinator: In the cupboard beside reception. You haven't used it before, have you?

Colleague: No, and neither has my colleague. Could someone show us how it opens?

Coordinator: I'll be checking equipment at nine. Join me then, and we can set it up together.

Colleague: Thanks. I was worried that asking basic questions would make us seem unprepared.

Coordinator: Asking now is preparation. It is much easier than discovering a problem while participants are waiting.

Colleague: Will you be working nearby during the session?

Coordinator: Yes, but I'll be taking calls for part of it. Write down the main instructions so you can manage without interrupting me every time.

sections.text:
The university observatory will welcome local schools next month. By the opening day, technicians will have installed a safer viewing platform and teachers will have received a short orientation guide. During the first evening, volunteers will be explaining the equipment while small groups wait their turn.

The publicity team was going to promise that every child would see Saturn. Astronomer Laylo objected. Cloud cover could prevent any outdoor observation, and even clear skies would not guarantee that every visitor could use the telescope at the best moment.

The revised programme includes an indoor activity using archived images. By the time each group leaves, pupils will have compared two observations and written a question for a researcher, regardless of the weather. They may still see Saturn, but learning will not depend entirely on that opportunity.

Some organisers worry that mentioning clouds will reduce bookings. Laylo argues that disappointment is more likely when an uncertain experience is advertised as certain. A clear alternative can make the visit more credible.

At the review meeting, the team will be examining pupil questions as well as attendance totals. A crowded evening will show demand; the questions may show what visitors noticed. By then, the team will have gathered evidence about both access and learning, rather than relying only on a photograph of a queue.

sections.transcript:
Project lead: What will your team be doing at three tomorrow?

Installer: We'll be attaching the final labels. By then, we will have positioned all the display cases, but the audio stations won't have been tested.

Project lead: Visitors arrive at five. Will you have finished the sound checks by four?

Installer: Yes, provided the recordings arrive tonight. We were going to use temporary files, but the curator said the final versions would be ready this evening.

Project lead: I need to distinguish a plan from a dependency. If the files are late, what can open safely?

Installer: The visual displays can. We can explain that the audio will follow, rather than play versions that contain errors.

Project lead: Good. By the time the doors open, we will have checked every public route as well.

Installer: Who will be recording any faults during the preview?

Project lead: Two volunteers. They won't be guiding groups; they'll be observing where people hesitate or ask for help.

Installer: That should tell us more than asking whether everything looks attractive.

Project lead: Exactly. We expect some adjustments. The aim is to identify them before regular visits begin, not to pretend that the opening proves the exhibition is finished forever.

Installer: I'll send a list of completed tasks and remaining dependencies after lunch.

sections.text:
The community learning centre is redesigning its end of course certificate. The old version stated that a learner had successfully completed the programme, but it did not explain what completion meant. Some learners attended every session; others missed classes but produced strong independent work.

The new certificate will describe participation separately from demonstrated skills. By the final meeting, each learner will have selected two pieces of work and explained one important revision. Teachers will be discussing those choices with learners rather than simply counting completed pages.

Although a single score would be easier to compare, the centre does not claim that its internal course provides an official examination result. A short profile can be more informative because it names the tasks completed and the support used. Everyone receives the same opportunity to present evidence, while individual strengths may differ.

The team was going to include a confident label for every skill. However, teachers recognised that some conclusions rested on only one task. Those areas will be described as needing further evidence.

A certificate should not promise more than the course has established. By the time learners leave, they should understand both what they can show and what they intend to improve. That makes the final document a useful record of learning rather than a decorative claim whose meaning nobody can explain.

sections.transcript:
Tutor: By Friday, you will have completed your community interview project. What will you be presenting at the final session?

Learner: I'll be showing two edited extracts and explaining why I changed the introduction. I was going to present the full recording, but it repeats several points.

Tutor: Could you tell me how you'll preserve the speaker's meaning while shortening it?

Learner: I'll keep the sentences that explain her main concern. Although the shorter version is easier to follow, I'll provide the complete transcript so that classmates can check the context.

Tutor: You haven't treated silence as agreement, have you?

Learner: No. She has approved the extracts, and I've recorded the changes she requested. I think the result is fairer now.

Tutor: So do I. What remains uncertain?

Learner: One interview cannot represent the whole neighbourhood. I'll say that clearly. I'm also thinking about interviewing someone with a different experience next term.

Tutor: Good. By the time the discussion ends, the class should have understood both your conclusion and its limits.

Learner: Will everyone be giving feedback during the presentation?

Tutor: They'll be taking notes first. Afterwards, each person will ask one evidence question. This is our internal learning review, not an official test score. The aim is to make your next decisions more thoughtful.

The proposed certificate separates participation from demonstrated skills. I support this because attending every lesson and producing effective work are related but different achievements. By the final meeting, each learner will have selected two examples and explained a revision, which gives the discussion a concrete basis.

A single score would certainly be easier to compare. However, convenience does not make a score more informative, especially when the course is an internal learning programme rather than an official examination. A short profile can identify the tasks and the support used without suggesting a wider guarantee.

During my final presentation, I will be explaining how feedback changed one piece of work. I will also acknowledge a skill for which I have too little evidence. Next term, I intend to collect examples from different situations so that my conclusions become more reliable.

A useful certificate marks a stage in learning. It should make the next step clearer instead of encouraging us to treat one successful task as proof that improvement is complete.

questions.prompt: Ikki muqobil tanlovni bog‘lang. Faqat mos so‘zni yozing: You may pay by card ___ use cash. (and / but / or)
